articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Detection and Classification of Multiple Sclerosis for Enhanced Patient Care
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a disease of the central nervous system that causes issues with the brain, spinal cord, and optic nerves. Multiple sclerosis affects an estimated 2.8 million people globally. Various forms of data, such as clinical and magnetic resonance imaging data, have been used to create a large number of MS diagnostic models. This work compares support vector machines, logistic regression, K-nearest neighbour, Naive Bayes, ensemble approaches (Adaboost, catboost, random forest, Light gradient boosting) for disease diagnosis and prediction. After comparing the outcomes of each classifier, it was found that Adaboost, LGB and Catboost Classifier exhibited the greatest and most dependable accuracy of 81.15%, 81.15% and 79.71 % respectively. Additionally, we discussed the difficulties and potential for developing AI systems for MS diagnosis, allowing practitioners and researchers to advance existing methods and automate MS diagnosis.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Approaches for Channel State Prediction in Heterogeneous Fading Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In this work, we leverage state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms to predict Channel State Information (CSI), for enhancing performance of wireless communication systems. The simulation and analysis stop with transfer learning to finetune, adaptive domain adaptations, multitasking (MTL) as well a few shot meta-learning models framework under different network packet loss rate scenarios. By generalizing better from one domain to another, transfer learning pushes the performance beyond what traditional methods can obtain. Further, fine-tuning also helps to align the source and target domain distributions in feature space by a partial (or full) reduction of re-stylization error. This work proposes multi-Task learning as a tool to mitigate loses in light of predicting across fading scenarios. Considering multi-task learning also provides benefits from shared learnings, so experience is pooled between the tasks which indirectly improve prediction as well and it helps in training both of these algorithms together. Moreover, the few-shot learning models prove to be highly desirable as they deliver state-of-the-art performance with minimal training data for difficult problems. These results show the potential of AI-based methods to improve CSI prediction, and have implications for improving reliability and throughput when deploying real wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Performance of Spatial Domain BGM Filtering and MS-SVM Classifier on Breast Cancer X-Ray Images Using CNN Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Over the decades, breast cancer has become one of the epidemic diseases among women throughout the universe that causes more mortality. Despite the evolution of many screening technologies, the mammogram is still considered the predominant screening tool to identify breast cancer at an earlier stage. As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to advance, many research investigations have been conducted into the automation process of breast cancer detection. This study shows how well a Markovian sample support vector machine (MS-SVM) classifier and a bilateral guided median (BGM) spatial filter work in a simulation model on a public x-ray dataset for breast cancer. The proposed MS-SVM classifier is used to train the breast lesion classification model as healthy or unhealthy tissues with the image features that have been extracted using the 5-layer convolutional neural network (CNN). In addition, for the evaluation of the MS-SVM classifier, traditional machine learning (ML) approaches such as SVM (support vector machine), RF (random forest), DT (decision tree), and NB (naive bayes) were used to analyze the classification metrics. Contrary to CNN and traditional ML classifiers, the proposed hybrid approach has improved accuracy by 0.987 with an increase in overall model performance of 5%, and the model training duration has been reduced to 157.27 seconds on average.

articleTitle: FinFET Based Design and Performance Analysis of Full Adders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Due to the rapid development of today's technology, the semiconductor circuit design method has faced many difficulties and problems. The full adder (FA) is a very large (VLSI) versatile device widely used for addition and subtraction in a variety of designs in signal processing (DSP) and integration. VLSI technology allows designers to place many gates on a single integrated circuit (IC). In this article, a FinFET-based full adder is designed and simulated using Cadence Virtuoso tools. We also compare the design with existing technology. Comparisons include the number of transistors, power consumption, and latency. From the simulation results, we clearly see that the design reduces power consumption and latency by 44 % and 68.3 %, respectively, compared to existing FinFET -based designs.

articleTitle: Arctangent Geman-McClure Based Chebyshev Functional Link Neural Network for Feedback Cancellation in Hearing Aids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach to nonlinear feed-back cancellation in hearing aids is proposed using the arctangent German-McClure Chebyshev functional link artificial neural network (AGMCFLANN). Conventional approaches to feedback cancellation typically utilize linear models, which may encounter difficulties in handling the nonlinearities present in hearing aid. This method intends to improve the network's accuracy in modelling complicated feedback dynamics by merging the arctangent cost function with the German-McClure approach within a Chebyshev functional link framework. Utilizing the arctangent function enables more effective management of nonlinear interactions, while the Chebyshev functional link improves the network's adaptability in modelling. An analysis has been conducted on the convergence of the proposed AGMCFLANN for feedback cancellation. Simulation results indicate notable enhancements compared to current feedback cancellation approaches. The proposed method demonstrates remarkable effectiveness in mitigating nonlinear feedback in terms of performance metrics such as added stable gain and improved speech quality.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Panel Maintenance: A CNN-GAN Approach for Dust Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The problem of dust settlement on solar panels is vital, likely decreasing their performance by 30%, which negatively affects energy yield and economic viability. Conventional dust detection approaches, such as optical sensors and basic image processing, frequently do not perform well in different environmental conditions. This investigation presents a pioneering hybrid framework that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to increase the detection and classification accuracy of dust on solar panels. CNN-GAN makes use of CNN's extraction of features and the data augmentation talents of GAN to create a sturdy structure that generalizes widely across multiple situations. The model was trained and assessed using an extensive dataset of 30,000 photos, divided into three categories: There is no Dust, some Light Dust, and a lot of Heavy Dust. This proposed model exceeded traditional models, including VGG-16 (accuracy of 89.2%) and InceptionV3 (accuracy of 90.5%), by achieving an accuracy of 95.4%. The CNN-GAN model suggested that accuracy stood at 96.2%, recall reached 94.7%, and the F1-score was an outstanding 95.4%. The Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC) was 0.97, implicating a powerful capability for discrimination. Investigations performed qualitatively indicated that pictures produced by GANs enhance CNN's educational process. The study points out the capability of the CNN-GAN model for immediate monitoring and automatic care of solar panels, ensuring maximum performance and energy efficiency. This research will also focus on expanding this methodology to reveal a larger range of abnormalities and implementing it into IoT devices for proactive maintenance solutions.

articleTitle: Literature Review: Recognization of Sign Language and Translation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive literature review on sign language recognition and translation, focusing on recognition of sign language and translating it into understandable text and vice versa. Translating devices act as a medium between sign language users and non-sign language users for understanding each other. This field, despite its significant advancements and profound impact on enhancing communication accessibility, yet it is not widely popular and still out of reach. In this review, we have analyzed up to 31 research papers published between 2010 and 2023 on different platform, discussing the methodologies, techniques, technologies, and models which resulted in successful creation of sign language translation systems. In this review we analyzed the research papers which showed significant results, however we cannot declare these research papers used as perfect, as each had its own weakness and strength. With this in depth review we can understand the most used methods, techniques, and their significances.

articleTitle: Towards the Machine Learning Techniques Based Network Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The relentless threat of network intrusion jeopardizes data integrity and privacy, posing a critical challenge in safeguarding digital assets and ensuring the stability of interconnected systems. Identifying and thwarting sophisticated intrusion attempts is a constant battle for cyber security. This research discusses and enhancing the efficiency of NIDS through the utilization of machine learning techniques, with a primary focus on Random Forest. The study compares the performance of Random Forest against prominent counterparts, including Gradient Boosting, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), using the NSL-KDD datasets. Through rigorous experimentation, Random Forest emerges as the front-runner, showcasing an impressive accuracy of 99.59%. The findings demonstrate the superior predictive capabilities of Random Forest in identifying and classifying network intrusions.

articleTitle: Paralysis Patient Health Care Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) have huge applications for the daily life improvement purpose. It also have wide applications on the medical field. There are many smart technologies introduced for the paralysed patients. As paralysis condition occurs because of loss of function of the muscle in the body parts. It can have the affect anytime resulting in not feeling any pain in the affected areas. There has been many technological and therapeutic ways to treat this condition. The objective of the work is to develop a smart medical devices for paralytic patients which can provide nursing care by using basic Healthcare monitoring system and should be available and affordable to common patients. A technology has been proposed that enables paralysed individuals to communicate their requirements through simple gestures in order to alleviate some of their problems. Through the integration of numerous sensors and devices, the system continuously gathers health data, giving users real-time insights into their vital signs and everyday demands. The proposed gadget can be attached with the patient cloth or it is also possible to attach with the finger of the patient. Finally the health condition will display on the LCD and simultaneously the data will get in smart phone through sms.

articleTitle: Interactive Touch Me Not Game: Arduino UNO and Closed Circuit Principles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This research paper explores the innovative integration of electronics and gaming by implementing a closed circuit current passing mechanism within the popular game “Touch Me Not” using the Arduino Uno microcontroller. “Touch Me Not” is a classic electronic game that challenges players to complete a circuit without touching the wire in the middle with the copper handle. Traditionally, this game relies on passive components like wires and metal contacts. In this study, we present a novel approach by incorporating the Arduino Uno platform to enhance the gameplay experience and educational value.

articleTitle: Transforming Pharmaceutical Drugs and Vitamin Classification: A Deep Learning Approach with CNN and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The paper considers the problem of classifying pharmaceutical drugs and vitamins using deep convolutional neural networks and transfer learning techniques. In this research, the dataset used contained images of some of the popular pharmaceutical drugs and vitamins available in the Philippines. This paper is primarily focused on the development of a robust image classification model that correctly identifies items based on their visual characteristics. In this work, we have used a deep CNN architecture that makes use of transfer learning; this has enabled us to make use of pretrained models for the classification task. The proposed model, applied to all classes, is very effective, with an accuracy of 84%. Individual class precision and recall scores both lie within the range of 0.74 to 0.94, while macro and weighted averages turn out to be 0.85 and 0.84, respectively. Notably, it did well in recognizing Medical with precision at 0.94 and recall at 0.95; this also turned in other commendable results across Bioflu, Decolgen, Fish Oil, and other categories. Results show that deep learning approaches have great potential in the domain of pharmaceutical classification and provide a starting point toward further advancements relating to automated drug and vitamin recognition. This work shall help to make more effective and precise pharmaceutical inventory management, therefore increasing consumer safety, as the right medicinal products will be identified and traced.

articleTitle: WSN Power Efficient Transmitter Using DG FINFET Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The study of WSN power-efficient transmitters (PETx) has been enhanced by the implementation of a more sophisticated description communication system. Double Gate FINFET (DGF) (Fin Shaped Field Effect Transistor) is used in WSN power-efficient transmitters (PETx), and it has been shown to be the mainly proficient in basis of transmitter frequency, low power consumption, and circuit development speed. A low power CPU interfaces the sensors and the PETx. The sensors and PETx are power gated to reduce standby power consumption. In deep submicron technology, circuit approaches to decrease leakage have been identified, and double gate FINFET has converse & functional on WSN power-efficient transmitters. Low power of PETx at 90nm technology has been calculated. In order to lower the power consumption of the WSN power-efficient transmitters, DG FINFET methods have been used. We look at how the DGF system, which uses transistors with the highest speed and lowest threshold voltage for PETx, provides low power and high presentation function.

articleTitle: Stand Alone or Non Stand Alone 5G Tactical Edge Network Architecture for Military and Use Case Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The advent of fifth-generation (5G) technology marks a paradigm shift in global communication infrastructure, transcending the incremental enhancements seen in previous generations. Far from being a mere upgrade in speed, 5G represents a holistic digital transformation, characterized by unprecedented multi-platform connectivity, advanced network slicing, and enhanced virtualization capabilities. As 5G continues to be deployed across India and internationally, the technology heralds the arrival of a unified communication network capable of supporting millions of concurrent devices with ultra-low latency and exceptional reliability. Unlike previous network generations, 5G is no longer defined solely by its throughput. Instead, it is poised to serve as the foundation for diverse services, encompassing both public and private networks. Within this ecosystem, two key deployment architectures emerge: 5G Non-Standalone (NSA) and 5G Standalone (SA). Each model offers unique advantages and challenges, necessitating a detailed evaluation of their respective capabilities to align with specific operational requirements, particularly in mission-critical domains such as military communications. Military communications, often built upon civilian technological frameworks, stand to benefit profoundly from the efficiency, precision, and enhanced decision-making afforded by 5G. The increased capacity, faster data transmission, and reliability inherent in 5G networks can dramatically augment the effectiveness of military operations and decision support systems. This paper undertakes a comprehensive performance evaluation of 4G/LTE, 5G NSA, and 5G SA architectures, with a focus on their applicability to military use cases. Leveraging simulations and key performance indicators (KPIs) derived from campus network studies, the analysis will critically assess whether these network configurations can meet the stringent requirements of military communications. The study will culminate in a recommendation for the optimal deployment strategy of a 5G network in military contexts, grounded in empirical data and performance metrics.

articleTitle: Stock Price Prediction Using Liquid State Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Predicting stock prices is a complex challenge, largely due to the unpredictable and fluctuating nature of market behavior. To address this issue, researchers have turned to Liquid State Machines (LSMs), a form of spiking neural networks, which are adept at capturing the intricate temporal patterns found in stock market data. The LSM model's ability to handle time-series information makes it suitable for analyzing historical stock trends to anticipate future market movements. In this study, the LSM was employed to forecast stock price changes, yielding promising results with a test loss of 0.9564 and a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.998 on the test dataset. These findings highlight the model's potential for financial forecasting, although further research is recommended to improve predictive performance by integrating additional data sources and refining the model architecture.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition from Facial Expressions Using Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Facial expression recognition is a crucial research area in computer vision with applications in human-computer interaction and affective computing. This study uses the KDEF and PICS datasets to develop an emotion recognition application leveraging deep learning techniques. A new model was created using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction. Deep learning models require extensive datasets for optimal performance. The KDEF dataset contains 4,900 images, while the PICS dataset has only 322 images. To address this limitation, data augmentation techniques were applied, expanding the PICS dataset to 4,830 images. Both datasets were then trained separately. The model classifies seven emotions: fear, anger, disgust, happiness, neutral, sadness, and surprise. It achieved 97.44% accuracy on the KDEF validation set and 98.24% accuracy on the PICS validation set.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Solutions for Early and Accurate Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Breast cancer remains a major global health concern, particularly for women. Early detection is essential for improved prognosis despite advancements in screening and treatment. Limitations of mammography, such as low sensitivity, necessitate exploring alternative approaches. Machine learning (ML) offers a promising solution with the potential to outperform traditional methods. This study investigates the potential of specific ML algorithms, including decision tree classifiers for interpretable results, random forest classifiers for improved accuracy, logistic regression for probability estimation, and support vector machines (SVMs) for optimal class separation for breast cancer detection using mammograms and other relevant patient data. Research suggests that these algorithms can achieve high accuracy and specificity, making them valuable tools to aid clinical decision-making, potentially leading to more accurate predictions, reduced unnecessary procedures, and personalized treatment plans. However, challenges persist, including the lack of standardized data collection and analysis protocols and non-diverse datasets that can limit model generalizability and introduce bias. Addressing these issues is crucial for robust model development. In conclusion, machine learning holds significant promise for improving breast cancer detection accuracy and efficiency, but further development and successful implementation rely on overcoming data standardization and diversity challenges.

articleTitle: A Time-Efficient Path Navigating Landmine Detection Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The goal of a landmine detection robot is to map the remaining area on a visual map with millimeter precision after covering as much ground as it can show landmines. The prototype land mine detection robot model described in this study offers a visual interface for mapping landmines, modifying PIDs, and aligning cameras. It is also reasonably powerful, accurate, and easy to operate with other sensors. The manual, semi-auto, and auto modes of controlling the differential drive robot are emphasized. Image processing determines the exact location of the robot and provides live reckoning feedback to its dead reckoning servo control. A beat metal detector is a kind of quiet sensor used to locate landmines. The overall objective of the system is to provide the user with something robust, affordable, and easily comprehensible for the user.

articleTitle: Enhanced Civilian Airport Detection with Optical Imaging and YOLOv9
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This project focuses on advancing civilian airport detection worldwide through the integration of optical imaging technology and the YOLOv9 deep learning architecture. Manual methods for identifying civilian airports using satellite images are slow, expensive, and prone to errors, posing challenges in urban planning, transportation management, and aviation security. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes an automated system that leverages high-resolution satellite imagery and advanced object detection algorithms. By integrating optical imaging data with the YOLOv9 model, this project enables quick and accurate detection and classification of civilian airports. With features including AI cameras, detectors, and automatic separators, this project offers a cost-effective approach to airport detection, catering to both large and small-scale facilities. By addressing the inefficiencies in current airport detection methods, this project aims to enhance, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness in civilian aviation surveillance and infrastructure planning.

articleTitle: Improving Orange Quality and Yield: A Smart Agriculture Framework for Ripeness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In agriculture, the detailed assessment of fruit maturity is vital, especially for oranges, because it powerfully affects the quality, market value, and endurance of fruits after harvesting. The presented work proposes a distinctive methodology that combines computer vision, machine learning, and IoT technologies to enhance and automate the precision of categorizing orange ripeness. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was created and trained using a dataset of 3,000 photos depicting three phases of ripeness: underripe, ripe, and beyond ripe. The model demonstrated an outstanding classification accuracy of 92 %, which exceeded the 75% accuracy of conventional strategies. The accuracy, recall, and F1-score for the CNN model were 91 %, 90%, and 90.5%, respectively, which outperforms the 73%, 72%, and 72 % provided by outdated approaches. The IoT element of the system made use of wireless sensors that continuously supervised environmental factors, including temperature, humidity, and soil moisture. The research study linking correlation found a considerable positive relationship between temperature and ripeness (r = 0.65, p = 0.01), suggesting real-time environmental data could significantly better harvest scheduling decisions. This complete strategy achieved a 15% increase in production quality along with a 10% drop in post-harvest losses. The findings showed that the suggested solution reduced labour expenditures by 30% and maintenance costs by 50% when considering traditional approaches, clearly illustrating that it is a viable detour for small and medium farms. Notwithstanding promising results, there is a need for further research to refine the applicability of the model in multiple orange varieties and different environmental circumstances. This research creates a framework for improving precision agriculture using ripeness assessment technologies.

articleTitle: X-FedLP: Explainable Federated Learning-Based Approaches for Link Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The rapid development of learning-based approaches in real life made Link Prediction a key network analysis tool. It has applications in social, biological, information, recommendation, and criminal networks. Many network applications require data security and privacy. Standard LP methods often lack scalability, privacy preservation, and interpretability. To overcome the constraints of standard LP approaches, this study offers Explainable Federated Learning-Based Link Prediction (X-FedLP) models, which integrate FL with XAI in LP. The revolutionary FL models FedNN, FedGNN, FedMF, and FedCF make up X-FedLP. These models are tailor-made for LP and deliver human-friendly results. X-FedLP models were tested using 5 real-world datasets, 3 evaluation criteria, and 8 performance assessment indicators. Prediction, performance, and interpretability are used to evaluate X-FedLP models. Tests show that FedMF and FedCF outperform FedNN and FedGNN.

articleTitle: Innovative Fare Collection Systems: Integrating IoT for Enhanced Urban Mobility and Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This research study examines the effects of IOT-enabled smart fare-collecting systems on urban transportation, emphasizing its operational, economic, and environmental advantages. The research assesses case implementations in Singapore, London, and New York City, using statistical techniques to measure the efficacy of these systems. The investigation indicates that IoT -based fare collecting may decrease operating expenses by an average of 12 % (p < 0.05) and improve service efficiency by 18% (p < 0.01) via optimized operations and decreased fee evasion. Furthermore, passenger satisfaction rates increased by 22% (p < 0.01) as a result of lowered waiting times and the ease of contactless payments. A comparison analysis of pre-and post-implementation data revealed a 30% reduction in cash handling and a 15% decline in ticket evasion occurrences, underscoring the financial and security advantages of smart fare systems. Furthermore, regression analysis revealed a substantial positive correlation (ß = 0.42, p < 0.05) between the use of IoT technology and the decrease in carbon emissions due to enhanced route planning and reduced congestion. Notwithstanding these benefits, hurdles like substantial initial investment expenditures and data privacy issues remain, with 64 % of surveyed cities seeing them as significant impediments. The results highlight the need for strategic planning and public-private collaborations to address these obstacles. This article indicates that IoT -enabled fee-collecting systems enhance operational efficiency and passenger happiness while promoting sustainable urban transportation, necessitating more research and development in this domain.

articleTitle: Enhancing Computational Model for Human Motion Recognition Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Human motion recognition (HMR) is a fundamental task in computer vision with applications in healthcare, surveillance, human-computer interaction, and intelligent environments. This paper proposes a better-performing model for HMR using VGG16 and starts the preprocessing on the diverse dataset of RGB images. Our meticulous process involves normalization, resizing, and then extracting images. These preparatory steps lay the foundation for robust model training. Exploration then takes two VGG16, EfficientNetB7 and ensemble VGG16-EfficientNet B7 deep learning architectures.

articleTitle: Optimizing GPS Positioning: A Deep Learning Approach to Improve Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In the pursuit of achieving unparalleled precision in position estimation, this study explores the capabilities of advanced deep learning architectures applied to dual-frequency Global Positioning System (GPS) data. Based on 22 hours of data collected at IISC Bangalore, our study assesses the efficacy of cutting-edge models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Bidirectional GRU (BiGRU), as well as Feedforward Neural Networks (FNN). By utilizing crucial performance indicators such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), R-squared (R2), and Explained Variance (EV), our thorough investigation reveals that LSTM models consistently surpass other architectural designs in performance, achieving the highest accuracy across the X, Y, and Z positional axes. These findings set a new benchmark for GPS signal processing, offering significant improvements in predictive performance. This study highlights the transformative potential of deep learning in navigation systems, with promising implications for autonomous navigation, geospatial analysis, and intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: EEG Based Driver Attention-Aware System for Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The number of road accidents has drastically increased over the years, with a significant proportion attributed to driver drowsiness, fatigue, and distraction. Many of these accidents could be mitigated by issuing timely alerts to drivers when they exhibit signs of drowsiness or distraction. Elec-troencephalogram (EEG) signals offer a viable approach for monitoring and analyzing a driver's cognitive and physiological states. In this paper, we propose a method for estimating drivers' eye states utilizing EEG signals. We employed a dataset captured using a 16-channel EEG headset, emphasizing features extracted from the alpha, beta, gamma, and theta frequency bands through windowing techniques. Initial models based on logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests yielded suboptimal accuracy. However, by integrating features across multiple frequency bands and implementing a real-time analysis approach using a sliding window combined with a majority voting strategy, we enhanced the prediction accuracy to approximately 90%. This demonstrates the potential of EEG-based eye state prediction for enhancing driver drowsiness detection and intervention systems.

articleTitle: SecretPixel: Advanced Steganography with Seeded Random Embedding and AES-RSA Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper presents SecretPixel, a steganographic tool that integrates random embedding techniques and advanced encryption to securely hide data within images. SecretPixel ensures confidentiality and integrity of the embedded data using AES-2S6 and RSA-4096 encryption algorithms. The Pixel Scattered Embedding (PSE) method hides encrypted information across image pixels, using a seeded random generator, enhancing resistance against steganalysis detection. This combination of two-tiered encryption, efficient compression and embedding strategies makes SecretPixel an effective solution for data concealment in digital communication.

articleTitle: Optimized Design and Analysis of Defected Ground Structure (DGS) MIMO Antenna for $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{u}^{-}}/\mathrm{K}$-Band Applications on Low Cost Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This article presents a simulated design and evaluated performance characteristics of two port DGS based MIMO antenna for the applications operating at Ku- band (12–18 GHz) and K-band (18-26.5 GHz). Initially, the single element antenna comprises of a numerically calculated rectangular patch fed through the X-Z plane truncated with two vertical rectangular slots on its left edge and dumbbell shaped slot at its centre. The partial ground structure is designed by incorporating the concept of DGS for wide band operational characteristics with the optimized umbrella shaped structural slots. The expansion of the design is ended for the two elements which are placed in an orthogonal manner for the augmentation of gain. The simulated two port MIMO design exhibits a peak gain of 6.28 dBi with 14-24.5 GHz impedance bandwidth along with 7.9 GHz gain bandwidth for >3dBi. Therefore, the anticipated 2x2 MIMO design is suitable for satellite communication system.

articleTitle: Design of 250 Gbps All-Optical Encryption and Decryption Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper presents an all-optical encryption-decryption circuit at a bit rate of 250 Gbps. The input signal is ciphered at the encryption side by utilizing an orthogonally polarized secure key. Cross-gain modulation is exploited inside the semiconductor optical amplifiers to cipher the input signal. The same key is used to decipher the encrypted signal at the decryption end by leveraging the cross-gain modulation in the SOAs. Decrypted signal quality is measured in terms of the eye diagram, quality(Q) factor and extinction ratio of the output. A high Q-factor and extinction ratio are achieved for the decrypted signal from this circuit, indicating its excellent performance.

articleTitle: Synergistic Fusion of CNN and BiLSTM Models for Enhanced Video Captioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In the realm of video captioning systems, the significance of leveraging CNN models for feature extraction cannot be overstated. These deep features, extracted from video frames, are seamlessly integrated with textual data features through a probabilistic matching approach, establishing crucial connections with the target text data. This study delves into the effectiveness of utilizing pretrained standard convolutional neural networks for feature extraction from video frames, with a keen focus on identifying the most suitable model to bolster video captioning systems. Through an exhaustive analysis, we explore various combinations of recurrent neural networks (RNN) with LSTM and GRU layers, coupled with the integration of Bidirectional layers, aiming to pinpoint nuanced model requirements for optimizing BLEU scores. Evaluation on the MSR- VTT dataset showcases notable enhancements, particularly when employing the MobileNet-V3 model for video frame feature extraction in conjunction with a BiLSTM-based model for subsequent text data processing. These findings culminate in substantial improvements in captioning outcomes, underscoring the potential of this integrated approach.

articleTitle: Optimized Pedestrian Detection Leveraging YOLOv9: A Thorough Deep Learning Framework for Autonomous Vehicle System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Pedestrian detection for an autonomous vehicle system is the crucial and foremost important aspect for accurate identification of pedestrian on the road scene environment. For this study a YOLOv9-C state-of-the-art deep learning model is used. YOLOv9 is renowned for its accuracy and efficiency in real time application. Model is trained on KITTI dataset. This dataset has a number of classes but for this study only pedestrian class is used. Dataset provides a number of images of urban scene environment where number of objects are there and trained model is perfectly detecting pedestrian in the images. In the YOLOv9 model an additional backbone layer is added for achieving high efficiency and time bound detection. The primary aim of this research is to look for the possible technique by which detection accuracy can be improved. Additional added layer helps in detecting more complex features of pedestrian in the images. After careful observation findings are shows that proposed model has achieved better accuracy in comparison with another models. Experimental results also show that there is a chance for more reliability and responsiveness of object detection if model is trained on diverse dataset. Although this study demands high computational resources which may be a barrier in some sense.

articleTitle: Antenna Designing Using Microstrip Technology for Anti Drone System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In this paper, a compact array triangular microstrip patch antenna design is proposed for C-band applications, as it is necessary to deploy an anti-drone system in the sensitive area to detect, locate, and defend against intruding drones. The proposed antenna is a high gain antenna with overall dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.45 \lambda\ \mathbf{x} 0.39 \lambda \ \mathrm{x}\ 0.03\ \lambda$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> is the operating wavelength. A gain of 5.5 dBi and 10.4 dBi is achieved by increasing the number of triangular radiating array of patches along with variation in material of substrate. The design of two different types of array antenna the linear two-element triangular array and the adjacent compact four-element triangular array has been discussed. The antenna structure is simulated using HFSS ver. 2022, measured using Anritsu Vector Network Analyzer and anechoic chamber, the simulated and measured results are in good concurrence. The antenna is suitable for radar and anti-drone system applications.

articleTitle: Streamlining Assessment with Dual T5-Models For QA-Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This study presents a new technique for solving question-generation and answer-generation tasks. Two T5 models are used to generate question-answer pairs from a given paragraph. The first T5 model generates questions, and the second T5 model generates answers. The objective is to develop a natural technique capable of generating multiple questions and answers. A dataset is gathered with three questions and three answers for each collected paragraph. Paragraphs are collected in three domains: “Renewable Energy”,”Environmental Science”, and “Pollution”. Using the two T5 models together aims to facilitate both questioning and answering while ensuring meaningful connections between the passages, questions, and answers. Users can also answer the questions generated by the first model and compare the similarity between their answers and the model's output. An average cosine similarity score of 0.73 was obtained for the first model, while the second model achieved a cosine similarity score of 0.74.

articleTitle: Smart Face Recognition System Using Hybridization of MTCNN and Facenet Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Face detection is a subfield of image processing that involves the identification of human faces from images or videos. Some common applications include facial recognition, emotion analysis, surveillance, and auto-tagging in photographs. Existing approaches suffer from less accuracy and high error. Therefore, a system with accuracy and precision is required to detect and identify the faces in real-time for security verification and surveillance. This paper aims to develop a face detection and recognition system. In this work, the Multi-task Cascaded Conventional Networks (MTCNN) algorithm is employed for face detection. It is a three-step convolutional network method, which is fast and accurate in detecting faces and obtaining the location of facial landmarks. Then, the FaceNet model is employed for face recognition. Once the faces are detected, the FaceNet model maps each face to a 128 vector, mostly preserving the distinct features of the face. These embeddings are further matched with a previously generated database to verify or find the person's possible identity. Extensive simulations have been conducted for performance analysis, and it was identified that the presented approach performs with improved accuracy compared to the peer methods.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Image Prediction Using Convolutional Neural Network Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This study provides an analysis of image prediction using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with varying kernel sizes using different image resolutions. The study inquires into four distinct models. Each of them with different combinations of convolutional kernels: Model-1 (3x3), Model-2 (3x3, 5x5), Model-3 (3x3, 5x5, 7x7), and Model-4 (3x3, 5x5, 7x7, 9x9). The models were assessed on images of three different sizes: 128x128, 64x64, and 32x32 pixels, and using the performance metric Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR),the predicted results are compared. It is uncovered that more the diverse the set of kernel sizes are, the better the model performs, irrespective of the image resolutions. The better the image resolution, the more information can be extracted from the images, which in turn gives better prediction accuracy. The highest PSNR values achieved are by Model-4 for all image resolutions, with 33.87 dB for 128x128, 28.12 dB for 64x64, and 25.86 dB for 32x32 images. This indicates that using a combination of kernels enables the model to capture both local and global image features more effectively, leading to improved prediction accuracy. In contrast, models with fewer or single kernel sizes exhibited significantly lower performance, particularly as the image size decreased. These results emphasize on the importance of multi-scale feature extraction in CNNs for image prediction tasks, suggesting that models with diverse kernel sizes are more robust and adaptable to varying image resolutions, how the image resolutions must be carefully selected for the relevant task. These insights have a great impact in practical applications like Reversible Data Hiding where image prediction is the major portion of the task and it's important to understand the appropriate kernel sizes, image resolutions, and appropriate number of images for the optimal prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Controller Design and Stability Analysis Using State Space Approach for Magnetic Levitation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In this research endeavor, the primary objective is to craft a dynamic nonlinear model for the Magnetic Levitation System. The proposed approach involves the development of both nonlinear and linear state-space controllers to enhance the system's control mechanisms. The linear controller is meticulously designed through the process of linearization around the equilibrium point. In contrast, the nonlinear controller is formulated following feedback linearization, wherein a nonlinear state-space transformation is adeptly employed to achieve an exact linearization of the system. For the linear controller, a full-state feedback approach is adopted. This design is then rigorously compared with its nonlinear counterpart, which incorporates a full-state feedback mechanism alongside a nonlinear observer. For drawing a conclusion on stability, a Lyapunov stability analysis was performed.

articleTitle: Advancements in Face Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Classifiers and Feature Extraction Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Face detection is a fundamental task in computer vision with applications spanning from facial recognition to surveillance systems. This research aims to advance the state-of-the-art in face detection by conducting a comprehensive comparative analysis of various classifiers and feature extraction methods across three different frameworks: OpenCV, TensorFlow, and Pillow. The primary focus is on evaluating the accuracy of classifiers, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and Decision Tree, when combined with feature extraction techniques such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and CASCADE, using different values of K as a parameter. The results reveal notable variations in classifier performance, with SVM consistently demonstrating high accuracy, particularly in combination with the CNN feature extraction method. Logistic regression also emerges as a strong performer across frameworks, while Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and Decision Tree show varying degrees of accuracy.

articleTitle: Real-Time Eye-Tracking Mouse Control System Using OpenCV and Facial Landmark Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The main goal of this project is to give people with disabilities, especially those who cannot use their hands, better access to computers by letting them control the cursor with eye movements. This project aims to precisely find where the pupil is within the eye using OpenCV technology. The pupil's position serves as a stable starting point for cursor control. The first step to reach this goal is detecting the center of the pupil by using a pupil detection process with OpenCV, as cursor movement is directly linked to it. By allowing people to control the cursor with their eye movements, the project wants to promote independence, inclusion, and equal participation in the digital world for people with impairments. In the end, the project hopes to provide easy and accessible ways for people with disabilities who cannot use regular input devices to interact with computers.

articleTitle: Towards Secure Hospital Data Systems: Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Integrity Management with AI and Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The research introduces a fresh hybrid architecture integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Blockchain technology to achieve real-time anomaly detection and to ensure data integrity in medical scenarios. The LSTM-CNN motivated model returned results of 95% accuracy and 94% F1-score along with 93% recall, underscoring its enhanced capacity for spotting both illegal data access and suspicious medical dealings. The experimental setup led to an analysis of a synthetic hospital dataset comprising 26,000 items, which included patient admissions, billing transactions, and medical records, with 5.3 % of the data specifically designed to include anomalies to assess the model's performance. After deploying the Blockchain on Ethereum, we ensured that the data was immutable and secure, completely removing cases of data tampering and unauthorized alterations, which descended from 5 and 8 incidents before the installation to zero following it. Also, the solution showed that reductions in validation failures went from 7 to 1, illuminating how smart contracts automate data validation processes. Results from latency studies demonstrate that the system is capable of managing real-time transactions with an average delay of 3.2 seconds, establishing its suitability for fluid medical environments that demand fast access to data. The research points out that the proposed framework may considerably increase data security and operational efficiency within healthcare contexts. The study generates a firm framework for developing more secure and trustworthy hospital data management systems, while future efforts will concentrate on enhancing the framework for broader deployment and improving its scalability to deal with increasingly complex healthcare data scenarios.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Lung Cancer Detection Using Relevant Feature and Neural Network Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Lung cancer is most common in men in India. Smoking is the main cause of lung cancer, apart from this there are many other reasons also. There are many tests to detect lung cancer such as chest X-ray and Computed tomography (CT). In this paper we are using two datasets to validate our work. First dataset-I is numeric data which is collectively based on surveys and second dataset-II contains CT images of lungs. In numeric data we have 15 features and have applied a neural network and ensemble classifier to classify the data into normal and cancerous classes. After that Pearson correlation method is used to select the most prominent features. The highest performance is obtained when the XGBoost ensemble classifier is used and the obtained values are Precision (95%), Recall (98%) and Fl score (96%). In the second dataset-II we have applied CNN to classify the lung images into multiple classes (normal, benign and malignant). But the accuracy is not prominent. Then we are using feature selection methods on flatten images and applying ensemble classifiers (Random forest, Gradient Boosting and Support Vector Classifier) to classify the images multiple classes. Prediction after feature selection is given a more prominent result and these are precision(1.00), recall(1.00) and F1 score(1.00).

articleTitle: Beam Steering of Single Microstrip Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper focuses on beam steering capability of a single microstrip patch antenna for fifth generation applications. The antenna is designed on RT-Duroid substrate of thickness 0.508 mm, dielectric constant of 2.2 and loss tangent 0.0009. The steering of beam by partially covered dielectric superstrate using dual slot radiation mechanism of microstrip antenna is used here. The proposed antenna-superstrate configuration acts as a two-element phased array resulting in beam tilt. The full wave simulations of this antenna-superstrate system using Ansys HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator) shows a beam tilt up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 32^{\circ}$</tex>, This method serves as an alternative to conventional method where multiple antenna elements with phase shifters were used, which are costly as well as lossy at mm wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Modified ResNet-101 Model for Enhancing Classification of Leukemia White Blood Cell Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Deep learning techniques will help classify and better identify acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The study aims to make tests more accurate and faster by using a light Modified ResNet-101 model and new ways to identify things like Yolo V5 and Yolo V8. The deep learning method is being used in the article to fix common problems in classification, such as slow convergence and poor generalization. Evaluation tools, such as the F1-score, accuracy, precision, and memory, are used to rate hoy well a model works. The proposed Modified ResNet-101 model correctly identified Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) cells 98.1 % of the time, which is better than most transfer learning models. Even better results are seen when Yolo V5 and Yolo V8 are used to find diseases.

articleTitle: Design and Development of In-Memory-Compute SRAM Cell Using 45nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The advances in the fields like IoT, AIML and Virtual Reality has demanded the extra fast computing. The same has been possible with development of hardware accelerators. For the computing, Von-Neumann architecture is the base for computing. The bottleneck in this system is data transfer between the processor and memory. To address these issues, the processing is now being brought closer to memory. Therefore, in this work, we design a 6T SRAM cell based In-Memory Computable SRAM macro (IMCSRAM) which performs logical operations in addition to memory read/write operation. In this paper, a 6T SRAM updated for in-memory-compute operation. This report presents the design of an Enhancement type 6T InCompute SRAM to augment computing capabilities. Leveraging n-well for writing operations and a differential read approach for reading, the circuit is implemented on a 45 nm technology node with a VDD of 1.1V. Implemented in a 45nm technology node with a VDD of 1.1 V, the circuit demonstrates a modest power consumption of 63uW. Notably, the proposed design supports various logic operations including AND, NAND, OR, and NOR, enhancing its versatility and applicability in diverse computing tasks.

articleTitle: Symptom-Based COVID-19 Detection: An Evaluation of Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In 2020, the global spread of COVID-19 posed significant challenges in distinguishing it from similar illnesses like allergies, colds, and flu due to overlapping symptoms. Traditional testing methods faced issues such as low accuracy and delayed results, particularly in developing countries. To address this, our research focused on distinguishing COVID-19 based on patient symptoms using various supervised learning algorithms, including decision trees, K-nearest neighbors, random forests, support vector machines, linear regression, and Naïve Bayes. Hyperparameter tuning via the grid search algorithm was used to optimize performance. Our experimental results indicate that these algorithms showed improved accuracy post-tuning. We have shown that result obtained from the proposed algorithm applied on various models. LR outperforms with an accuracy of 96.023 than other Machine Learning models This approach could facilitate rapid detection and classification of illnesses with similar symptoms, aiding in the prompt management and containment of COVID-19.

articleTitle: Refined YOLOv8 for Enhanced Small Object Detection in PCB Defect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In the electronics industry, the timely and accurate detection of defects in printed circuit boards (PCBs) is crucial for maintaining high standards of product quality and efficiency. Tra-ditional methods often struggle with identifying small and subtle defects, leading to the need for more advanced approaches. This paper presents an enhanced version of the YOLOv8 model tai-lored for PCB defect detection. The proposed model incorporates several key modifications: the use of He initialization and batch normalization to improve network stability and convergence, and a learnable parameter for better feature fusion. The loss function was adapted to emphasize small object detection, which is critical for identifying minute defects. Extensive experiments on a comprehensive PCB defect dataset demonstrate that the modified YOLOv8 model significantly outperforms the standard version, offering a practical solution for real-time, high-precision defect detection in industrial applications. Experimental results demonstrate the model's superior performance, achieving a precision of 95.95%, a recall of 97.74%, and a mean Average Precision (mAP50) of 98.32%. These improvements make the enhanced YOLOv8 model highly effective for real-time PCB defect detection in industrial settings, offering a robust solution for quality assurance processes.

articleTitle: IoT Sensor-Based Monitoring of Fish Diseases in Aquaculture: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Aquaculture plays a vital role in meeting the growing global demand for seafood. However, traditional aquaculture practices face challenges such as water quality imbalance, frequent fish diseases, and labor shortages. This review paper examines the correlation between various water quality parameters and their impact on the health of Indian Major carp in aquaculture systems, with a focus on disease development. Key parameters discussed include dissolved oxygen (DO), temperature, total dissolved solids (TDS), pH, salinity, conductivity, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide, nitrites, nitrates, phosphorus, chlorine, total suspended solids (TSS), and carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The review emphasizes the importance of regular monitoring and maintaining these parameters within optimal ranges to minimize disease outbreaks and optimize fish growth. A comprehensive analysis of water quality literature from 2014 to 2024 was conducted using digital databases such as IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and Web of Science. The study highlights research gaps in the accuracy of models, development of data-gathering systems, and types of data used in proposed frameworks. By understanding the complex relationships between water quality and fish health, aquaculture practitioners can implement effective management strategies to enhance the sustainability of aquaculture systems. The review concludes by identifying critical topics for future research and presenting research directions towards smart water quality management in aquaculture.

articleTitle: Secrecy Capacity Optimization in RF/FSO Systems: Impact of Mixed Rayleigh and Log-Normal Fading with Atmospheric Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper investigates the secrecy capacity optimization in RF/FSO systems with mixed Rayleigh and log-normal fading, while masking eavesdroppers channel state information () as well as suffering from atmospheric turbulence. We explore the impact of several parameters including beamforming angles, modulation schemes and hybrid RF/FSO link configurations through a combination of simulations as well as analytical models. Secrecy capacity is enhanced for an improved SNR and vice versa under higher turbulence conditions and cooler influents eavesdropped scenarios. Performance of the hybrid RF/FSO systems dominates considerably over single-link solutions, especially at longer distances. All these mechanisms appreciably increase the secrecy capacity, while beamforming and advanced modulation techniques offer most of the improvement. The study also demonstrates the interdependencies of system parameters, providing guidelines for designing secure communication systems under different environmental and operational conditions.

articleTitle: Enhanced Skin Lesion Classification Using CNN and Fine-Tuned VGG16 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Skin cancer is a prevalent form of cancer globally, necessitating accurate and early diagnosis. Leveraging deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), has shown promise in dermatological applications. This paper presents a skin lesion classification approach using VGG 16, enhanced through fine-tuning for dermoscopic images, extensive data augmentation, and a weighted loss function to address dataset imbalance and improve performance on minority classes. It also utilizes a balanced dataset from the HAM10000. VGG16 is a widely recognized convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, designed by the Visual Geometry Group at the University of Oxford. It gained prominence for its outstanding performance in image classification during the 2014 ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge(ILSVRC). We utilize the pretrained VGG16 model's initial weights as the starting point for the convolutional layers in our proposed architecture. The experiments are conducted on an Nvidia T4×2 GPU to accelerate the results. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 85.12 % for skin lesion classification.

articleTitle: Elevating IoT Efficiency: Fusing Multimodal Data with Federated Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The increasing use of smart elements in some industries generates high amounts of complex data, which challenges data privacy and scalability processing. This work presents the Multimodal Federated Learning (MFL) framework designed to leverage multimodal input data in a decentralized manner while preserving users' privacy. We assessed the suggested architecture using three authentic IoT datasets. The three main categories that it covered include Healthcare, Smart City, and Autonomous Driving. The MFL framework displayed exceptional performance, achieving an overall accuracy of 90% over all the datasets, with specific accuracies of 92 % in Healthcare, 88% in Smart City, and 90% in Autonomous Driving, a performance that is 12 % above the normal Federated Learning models. The results have been quite impressive, and the precision and recall scores are high: precision 91 %, 87%, and 89%, and recall 90%, 86%, and 88% for the respective datasets. The F1-Score achieved by the framework is as follows: Healthcare modality scored 90.5%, Smart City scored 86.5%, while the Autonomous Driving modality score was 88.5%, which shows the framework's effectiveness in many modalities. The MFL framework successfully reduced the COM overhead by 30% for Healthcare, which needed only 500 MB; Smart City needed 400 MB, while Autonomous Driving needed 450 MB in comparison to the 700 MB, 600 MB, and 650 MB taken by other centralized learning approaches. The study demonstrated that the MFL can integrate different IoT data into one set without violating data privacy and at an affordable communication cost, making it possible to provide security measures for implementing scalable and complex IoT environments using the machine learning algorithm.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Traffic Law Enforcement: IoT-Enabled Vehicle Control Systems for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This article presents an enhanced Internet of Things-based vehicle management system for traffic law enforcement to improve road safety and compliance with the law. The designed system will integrate real-time data collection from various IoT devices such as cameras, speed sensors, and RFID readers and incorporate complex machine learning algorithms to detect offences on the road and control the traffic patterns accordingly. In a three-month prototype application in a small metropolitan area, the system demonstrated a traffic violation detection rate of 92.3% - including speeding and red-light running - with a reduction of false positives compared to traditional methods of 28%. Upon putting the system to use, releases in traffic violations were cut by 30%, and the punctuality of the traffic flow during rush hour was given a 15% boost with evidence of the reduction of average waiting time at major junctions. Furthermore, it enhanced the response time via technology, with responders achieving an 18% cut in the average response time of emergency vehicles compared to the original method. Nevertheless, some problems were observed: first, high dependence on the Internet - the data processing of objectives was slowed down by 12% of regions with a weak Internet connection. In addition, 14 % of users reported concerns about data privacy, showing the necessity of taking steps to improve data protection. The results reveal that while the IoT -based vehicular control system yields benefits for enforcing traffic laws, key challenges relating to connectivity, the privacy of information, and system adaptability must be addressed if it is to be first applied and then effectively implemented in extensive urban environments.

articleTitle: A Graphene FET Based Wideband Power Amplifier at D-Band for High-Speed Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This work presents a Graphene Field Effect Transistor (GFET) based D-band power amplifier for high-speed applications. By establishing a proper input and output microstrip line (MSL) matching networks a wideband of20 GHz is achieved by cancelling the harmonics at higher frequencies. A two-stage CS topology with inter-stage coupling is employed to achieve a gain of 21 dB. This wideband power amplifier (P A) achieves an output power Pout and drain efficiency of 20 dBm and 75%, respectively.

articleTitle: Compact Design and Analysis of Microwave Band Pass Filter using Coupled Lines with Four Reflection Zeros for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the compact design and study of a microwave band-pass filter (BPF) consisting of two transmission and four reflection zeros for modern 5G communication systems. The demonstrated BPF is structured with three coupled lines. The filter's circuit and electromagnetic (EM) simulations were conducted using Ansys Electronics Desktop. The S-parameters of the filter were derived using the even-odd mode method to extract mathematical equations for the transmission and reflection zeros of the presented BPF. This compact BPF, consisting of center frequency 2.5 GHz, was developed and simulated, achieving an optimal 3-dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 68.76%, a fall-off rate of 87.2 dB/GHz, an insertion loss of greater than 60 dB in its stop band, return losses greater than 12dB in its passband and a selectivity factor (SF) of 0.91. The circuit and HFSS design simulated results are in acceptable match.

articleTitle: Predictive Maintenance of Railway Tracks Using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Railway tracks are the most prominent base of train movement, any defect in the track may lead to minor/major unhappening. To minimize risk and maximize safety, regular maintenance or condition-based maintenance must be performed. In this paper, a deep learning-based algorithm is proposed for automatic fault detection in railway tracks using LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory). LSTM model, an advanced version of recurrent neural networks known for their accuracy are compared with existing Deep Learning techniques to identify common railway faults, such as defects in rails and fasteners. Predictive maintenance is used to perform required maintenance before the failure of tracks by estimating RUL (Remaining Useful Life) of tracks and their components. This Proposed model is applied to the trusted source dataset which detects three defect types (DIP, XLEVEL, SURFACE). This approach enhances proactive maintenance, reduces downtime, optimizes schedules, and improves railway system reliability and safety. Our research advances predictive maintenance practices, showcasing how LSTM networks can transform railway infrastructure maintenance strategies.

articleTitle: Incremental Strategy Based ANC Using Hybrid Adaptive Nonlinear Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The prevalence of nonlinearities in adaptive filters poses a challenging issue for noise reduction. Several methods are introduced to enhance the effectiveness of distributed active noise control (DANC) systems while dealing with nonlinearities. In this context, DANC algorithms utilizing Mish functions are being proposed to address noise reduction challenges. The Mish function addresses the issue of the vanishing gradient problem and enhances the speed at which convergence occurs by leveraging the smoothness and unboundedness characteristics. Considering this, the present manuscript introduces a collection of nonlinear methods for the DANC system that employs the Mish framework into an incremental strategy for filtered-x least mean fourth (IMF-xLMF) and filtered-x least mean square (IMF-xLMS). The proposed approaches entail designing weight update equations specific to the developed algorithms and performing a comprehensive convergence analysis. The suggested methods yield a quantitatively significant gain of 1–4 dB in noise reduction, effectively handling nonlinearities and reference signals, all while converging faster than previous techniques.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Controlling Greenhouse Parameters by using IOT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Agriculture is the primary occupation in our country. But there are currently obstacles in agriculture because of the migration of people from rural to urban areas. Therefore, we use Internet of Things-based smart agriculture solutions to solve the issue. This Paper includes the concept of internet of things (IoT) for Monitoring and controlling the different Parameters of greenhouse farming. The different parameters such as Temperature, humidity and Moisture percentage inside the soil are monitored for healthy crop production. Technological advancements are crucial in the agriculture business since they conserve time and labour. The created system comprises a mix of Arduino and several sensors to monitor greenhouse data in real time. The technology collects real-time crop data via sensors and transmits it to the user's mobile device. The user may monitor and regulate the temperature, lighting and irrigation in the greenhouse using a mobile smartphone.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz Low-Noise Amplifier with Pseudo Feed-Forward Active Neutralization Suitable for Multi-Stage Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This article presents a cascode low-noise amplifier (LNA) design featuring active neutralization technique suitable for performance improvements in multi-stage topologies. A feed-forward path consists of series of active devices that imparts small or tiny gain is proposed to compensate losses in cascode amplifier. Active devices that envelop on commonsource and common-gate configurations are utilized properly for performance improvements. At the center frequency of 60 GHz, the proposed designs exhibit the gain increments of 9.3 dB and 7.1 dB with 1 mW less power when compared to conventional multi-stage LNA. The proposed work is based on 65-nm CMOS technology that gives minimum noise figure of 4.791 dB while the input and output reflection coefficients are almost less than -20 dB.

articleTitle: Towards U-Net Based Semantic Segmentation for Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Semantic segmentation in satellite imagery is a critical process that involves categorizing each pixel into pre-defined classes such as buildings and roads. The challenge lies in developing accurate automated methods capable of efficiently classifying and mapping diverse types of land cover. Traditional approaches work very well on sample data. However, with a change in the data set, performance was found to be limited. In this direction a semantic segmentation based deep learning architecture, U-Net with ResNet having versions 50, 101, and 152 has been considered which helps to find the significant feature. For this research, Landcover.ai and Dubai landcover dataset have been used, which contains high-resolution images annotated with classes buildings, roads, land, water, and forests. Adam optimizer and Jaccard loss function were considered to train our model with data augmentation. Our experiments demonstrated that this approach achieves a mean IoU score of 80.20% and 82.95% in the test data set.

articleTitle: Customized Obstacle Dataset Generation from RGB-D Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The field of Obstacle Detection in computer vision is evolving rapidly, with many researchers contributing innovative solutions to address different challenges. However, the current landscape presents several barriers that hinder effective comparison and collaboration among researchers. A significant challenge arises from the limited availability of publicly accessible obstacle datasets, with existing datasets predominantly focused on specific contexts such as obstacles on roads, sidewalks, or particular industrial settings. The varied application contexts, environments, and hardware equipment in use compel researchers to develop and use custom datasets tailored to their application-specific requirements. Constraints such as time, funding, and limited access to resources often discourage researchers from re-creating new datasets for the purpose of comparative evaluations, resulting in incomplete insights into the strengths and weaknesses of different approaches. To address this deficiency in comparative analysis, we propose a novel method for generating obstacle datasets from existing RGB-D datasets dynamically. The proposed method offers a quick and effortless way to generate customized variants of Obstacle dataset, without having to manually build them from the ground up. The cross-dataset compatibility of the proposed method further enhances the versatility and wide adoption potential of the proposed method.

articleTitle: FireNet: A Transfer Learning Approach for Robust Fire Detection with Pre-Trained CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Detection of fires is crucial in preventing massive loss and ensuring safety in various areas. This study examines transfer learning with pretrained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for fire detection through images and compares the results to tailored YOLO models for real-time object detection. We employed the VGG16, ResNet50 and Inception V3 models trained for a specific fire detection dataset, and the accuracy achieved was 93. 4%, 95. 6%, and 94. 8%, respectively. On the ResNet50 model, the performance was impressive, making an accuracy of 0. 96 out of a total of cars with a recall rate of 0. 95, a recall of 0. 86, and an F1 score of 0. 96%, making it the most successful model of this kind of job.
