InceptionV3 and VGG16 proved to be up to the mark where Inception V3 achieved a precision of around 0. 95, recall of 0. 94 and F1 score of 0. 95, and even better results were obtained by FCA- VGG, with a precision of 0. 93, recall of 0. 93 and the F1 score of 0. 93. On the other hand, YOLOv4, which is a real-time identification model of objects achieved a performance of 94.5%, the precision of 0. 94, recall of 0. 93, and the precision of the F1 score is 0. 94, which makes it ideal for contexts which require fast detection. YOLOv3 showed 93% accuracy., precision of 0. 92, recall of 0. 91, and F1 score of 0. 92 % or slightly behind.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Intake Activity Recognition Using KNN Through FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has found many practical applications in various fields, including human-computer interaction, health assessment, and smart surveillance. The resilience of radar sensors to environmental factors makes them well-suited for recognizing human activities. As a sensing modality for HAR, radar offers unique advantages like privacy protection and contactless monitoring. This paper proposes a fine grained intake HAR using K-nearest neighbor (KNN) through frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar. The over-lapped windowing is utilized for radar signal segmentation. The time domain-based features are applied to each window frame for the classification process. The classification process is evaluated utilizing classifiers such as DT, SVM, and KNN for 2-class and 3-class classification. The KNN classifier outperform various selected classifiers for radar-based HAR for 3-class classification. Comparative performance is performed utilizing 4 different cases. The overall classification accuracy of Case-1, Case-2, Case-3, and Case-4 using KNN are 98.83%, 98.98%, 99.59%, and 98.84% respectively. Further, classwise performance has been evaluated for Case-1 (3- class) providing the macro-average accuracy, precision, sensitivity, F1-score as 99.22%, 97.72%, 97.94%, and 97.83%, respectively.

articleTitle: Energy and Area Efficient 16-Bit Approximate Multiply-Accumulate (EAMAC) Architecture for Error Tolerant Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Approximate computing has become a viable method for achieving major power and energy savings in computer systems in recent years. It is frequently used in computationally demanding, fault-tolerant systems that requires complex arithmetic blocks. Applications that require convolution operations, such as image processing and convolutional neu-raL networks (CNN), frequently use the Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) unit. This paper proposes an energy and area efficient approximate multiply-accumulate (EAMAC) architecture for error resilient applications. The proposed EAMAC architecture simultaneously introduces approximation in the accumulation and multiplication stages. The proposed EAMAC architecture uses an Approximate Multiplier based on the Modified Booth Encoding (MBE) technique and Wallace Tree reduction for the multiplication stage and carry select unit-based accuracy con-figurable approximate adder (CSU-ACA) for the accumulation stage. The experimental results show that the proposed EAMAC architecture when implemented on Kintex-7 Field Programmable gate Array (FPGA) reduces power, area, and delay by 44.5%, 27%, and 32.5% respectively as compared to the exact MAC architecture implementation. EAMAC shows an energy-efficiency of 62% with high PSNR and EQ quality metrics when demonstrated on image smoothing application showcasing the design suitability for error tolerant applications.

articleTitle: Spatial Dynamics for Identification of Individuals through Gait and Other Locomotion Activities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Gait, the pattern of walking, has been extensively studied and various methods have been developed to use it as a biometric for individual recognition. Despite this, the potential to identify individuals through running videos has not been thoroughly explored. The paper introduces a novel method that expands the feature-based approach for identifying individuals based on their running style. This work focuses on extracting the mutual information and location specific metric from the key gait poses of subjects in the testing and training datasets. Later on, the assignment of a testing sample to the training sample is accomplished using the proposed classification method. The experiments are conducted on KTH, OU-ISIR A, and Weizmann database. The efficiency of this method is demonstrated by the obtained experimental results.

articleTitle: Optimizing Automated Eye Disease Detection: A Deep Learning Approach Using EfficientNetB3 for Accurate Multi-Class Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of eye diseases such as cataract, diabetic retinopathy, and glaucoma is a big public health concern. Due to this main reason, early diagnosis has become highly important for people to prevent vision loss. This work will apply deep learning for automating eye diseases with classifications using an EfficientNetB3 model, enjoying a good balance between accuracy and computational efficiency. It was trained and evaluated on a dataset of 4,217 images of retinal fundus, representing the classes normal, cataract, glaucoma, and diabetic retinopathy. Indeed, after the adoption of image augmentation, class weighting, and fine-tuning, the accuracy of classification reached as high as 93%, with good precision and recall in all classes. These results are indicative of the robust performance of the model, while the identification of the cases with diabetic retinopathy and cataract showed very high accuracy. Glaucoma and normal conditions enjoyed good accuracy. This study has identified that autodeep learning models can play a possible role in aiding ophthalmologists with early diagnosis for better diagnostic accuracy and for better patient outcomes in clinical use.

articleTitle: Extreme Learning Machine-Based Unified Voice Spoofing Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Spoofing attacks like the replay (i.e., using recorded voice of bonafide speaker), and cloning (i.e., using state-of-the-art Text-to-Speech for cloning bonafide voice and using) can be applied on various voice-assistant-enabled systems, voice-based biometrics, etc. Most of the existing countermeasures perform well on only specific attacks and thus fail to generalize for other classes of spoofing attacks. In this paper, an audio spoofing architecture using extreme learning machine (ELM) techniques is developed. Features such as acoustic local ternary patterns and gamma tone cepstral coefficients (GTCC) are employed. The performance of ELM is compared with Gaussian Naïve Bayes, decision tree classifier, and support vector machine (SVM) on the ASVspoof2019 dataset. It has been demonstrated in the result section that the proposed ELM-based spoofing detection system outperformed over mentioned schemes and achieved the highest accuracy of 99.2% with the lowest equal error rate value of 0.2% at a lower computation time.

articleTitle: Sparse Channel Estimation in Massive MIMO Systems Using Compressed Sensing and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In this paper, based on compressed sensing and neural networks, we present an intelligent sparse channel estimation technique for Massive MIMO systems. We show that our approach improves considerably the estimation accuracy in terms of Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE) with respect to classical methods. We demonstrate [Figure: ] that our approach is computationally more efficient, requires less time and resources (memory/disk) compared to the existing literature but for a robustness of performance across distal or low Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs). We also confirm our method exhibits fast convergence and efficiently accommodates a variety of sparsity levels. By visualizing it using heatmaps and ROC curves we show that this method is able to effectively differentiate between signal and noise, asserting our approach as a powerful tool for the contemporary set of problems present in wireless communications.

articleTitle: Towards Road Anomaly Detection for Autonomous Vehicle System Using Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Safety on road is still the top priority, despite the development of intelligent as well as autonomous car technologies brought about by recent advances in automobile technology. A move towards vision-based sensors and deep learning approaches for better scene interpretation has been prompted by the high costs and patchy performance of conventional sensors like radar and LiDAR for the safety of vehicles. It is crucial to detect road irregularities accurately, like potholes and speed bumps Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are optimized for improved anomaly detection in this research study, the accuracy and performance of the model have been improved by carefully regulating the batch size and experimenting with various optimizers a dataset of 1900 labeled photos was used to test the CNN architecture which was modeled around LeNet-5 the adam optimizer was used for fine-tuning resulting in a detection accuracy of 94.2% and using common assessment matrices, the suggested model's performance is verified. This optimized approach enhances safety and reliability in autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Leveraging Xgboost for Accurate Prediction of Chronic Kidney Disease with Real-Time Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) poses a significant threat to public health, necessitating early diagnosis and continuous surveillance to avert severe consequences. This study utilizes machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and XGBoost, to predict CKD using a unique dataset comprising 2,752 patient records sourced from real-time data including 2,221 CKD patients and 531 non-CKD patients. The dataset features 28 significant attributes, including three clinical tests: Basic Urine Routine, Urinary Microalbumin Creatinine Ratio, and Kidney Function Test. To ensure reliable model evaluation, a 10-fold cross-validation method was implemented. Among the algorithms, XGBoost delivered the highest performance, achieving an accuracy of 98.53%, a precision of 99.20%, a recall of 98.53%, and an F1 score of 98.76%. Random Forest followed closely behind with 98.31% accuracy, 99.10% precision, 98.31% recall, and a F1 score of 98.59%. SVM also displayed strong performance, attaining 94.18% accuracy, 98.89% precision, 94.18% recall, and an F1 score of 96.07%. These findings underscore the superior accuracy of XGBoost in predicting CKD and highlight its potential for integration into clinical settings to improve early identification and management, ultimately improving patient outcomes and reducing clinical expenses.

articleTitle: A Non-Linear Detector Based on Linear Techniques for MUD in Acoustic Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: High-rate communication in acoustic environment is achieved using multiple input multiple output (MIMO) combines with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) scheme. But, the capacity of such system degrades due to multiple access interference (MAI). Therefore, symbol detection for such system is achieved using multiuser detection (MUD) in acoustic communication. In this research, MUD is accomplished in underwater acoustic (UWA) environment using weighted parallel interference cancellation (WPIC) technique based on zero-forcing (ZF) and minimum-mean-square-error (MMSE) detector. The channel modelling incorporated in the system is based on singular value decomposition (SVD). The outputs resulted from MATLAB simulation reveal that proposed method achieve good system performance and also MMSE detector outperform over ZF detector in bit error rate (BER) performance.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Sub-Type Classification in Ovarian Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Ovarian cancer is a significant public health concern, ranking as the eighth most frequent cancer in women worldwide. However, it is more prevalent in some regions, such as India, where it is the fourth most common cancer in women. It poses a significant risk due to its high fatality rates, which are related to late-stage diagnosis. Early identification of ovarian cancer is challenging, owing to its diverse nature, which includes numerous subtypes with overlapping characteristics. Furthermore, traditional histological diagnosis, which is based on tissue samples, is time-consuming and subject to interobserver variability among pathologists. Given these intricacies, we have proposed a novel approach that can classify the sub-type classification of endometrial ovarian cancer using pre-trained models like VGG19 and EfficientNetV2. The experimental results discern the potential of models to overcome these limitations and achieve a more accurate and efficient sub-type classification of endometrial and ovarian cancer and could significantly improve early diagnosis and pave the way for personalized treatment strategies.

articleTitle: BERT-Based Nepali Grammatical Error Detection and Correction Leveraging a New Corpus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Nepali GEC plays a crucial role in improving the quality of written Nepali text. An annotated corpus of Nepali sentences along with sentences generated by augmenting correct sentences to generate a diverse range of grammatical errors are used for training. The augmentation is done by identifying the Part of Speech tag and root words of verbs and adjectives using Lemmatizer. This study uses BERT models MuRIL and NepBERTa to fine-tune for the GED task of Nepali text. The models performances were assessed using accuracy and training/validation loss, providing a comprehensive assessment of the model's effectiveness in error detection for the Nepali Language which forms the crucial step for GEC. The GEC system developed here, makes use of MLM models of both MuRIL and NepBERTa to predict the mask tokens in input erroneous sentence and thus gives the suggestions which are filtered by the GED model.

articleTitle: Interconnection of LoRa Based IoT Nodes on 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: 5G along-with loT are two of the most disruptive technologies shaping modern innovation, particularly in the realms of connectivity, sensing, and communication. Their convergence holds immense potential to unlock diverse opportunities, particularly for advanced applications in smart cities. 5G, as a next-generation network, is fully virtualized and designed for seamless integration with non-3GPP technologies, while loT operates as an expansive, low-power ecosystem optimized for sensing and actuation. However, loT's constrained transport capabilities and inherent security vulnerabilities, owing to its low-power architecture, present notable challenges. Before integrating Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWAN) with 5G, it is crucial to address security concerns, especially those related to authentication and the seamless roaming of loT devices across 5G networks. The integration of these technologies is expected to drive significant advancements in smart city infrastructure and beyond, but robust solutions must be developed to overcome the inherent risks. This paper advocates for leveraging existing cellular network authentication frameworks, obfuscating device identities to enhance privacy, storing authentication credentials within home networks to mitigate roaming-related issues, and employing loT gateways to manage device address translation. By implementing these strategies, a secure and seamless integration of 5G and loT can be realized, laying the foundation for a more connected, resilient, and secure future. Additionally, this convergence will facilitate the deployment of Internet of Battlefield Things (loBT) for surveillance-centric applications, broadening the scope of both civilian and defense-related use cases.

articleTitle: An IoT Based IoT Framework to Forecast PM10 Concentrations in Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The state of outdoor air pollutants is known to strongly influence indoor air. The correlation between inside and outside pollution concentration time series has been used to develop an edge computing based IoT system which estimates the indoor PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>concentration on the basis of the outdoor PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>concentration of that locality. There are about 35 air quality monitoring stations in different parts of Delhi which provide details about the outdoor PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>levels of the locality. Forecast model has been developed for assessing indoor PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>concentration with the help of the current outdoor PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>concentration time series using recurrent multiplicative neuron artificial neural network (RMN-ANN). The performance of the model has been assessed by average absolute deviation (AAD), root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) metrics. The RMN-ANN based forecast model has been found to be the accurate with a MAPE of 1.89% and an RMSE value of 10.26μg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Channel Prediction in Non-Stationary Wireless Fading Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In non-stationary wireless fading channels deep learning models are effective in predicting channel states as indicated by this study. This work compared the LSTM and GRU models with autoregressive methods or Kalman filter, implying that deep learning is indeed able to capture temporal dependence between variables and was likely more adapted than linear method when dealing with many changes in dynamics. From the perspective of pre-processing data, keys like attention mechanism and transfer learning were decisive elements in helping them to improve prediction scores and make models more robust. These results showed that these enhanced procedures allow the models to generalise over a wide range of non-stationary situations, generating consistent performance in various diverse environments. This study indicates the promise of deep learning for enhancing wireless network operation, which could lead to greater self-awareness and utilization features in emerging future-generation wireless systems.

articleTitle: Low Profile Wideband 3 Element Parasitic Hexagonal Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: A low profile 3-element hexagonal parasitic patch antenna is presented. Initially, a coaxial-fed circular patch antenna (CPA) is designed on the Rogers 4350B substrate of 60 mm x 60 mm. The bandwidth of CPA is measured at 80 MHz. This CPA is then converted into a single hexagonal patch antenna and later converted into a 3-element parasitic hexagonal patch (PHP) antenna. The final 3-element parasitic hexagonal patch antenna covers a bandwidth of 375MHz with 2 resonance frequencies. The gain of the proposed antenna improved to 7.5dBi and 8.71dBi as compared to reference CPA with a gain of 5.01dBi. The improvement in bandwidth and gain is the result of 2 hexagonal structures placed near the main radiator. The proposed antenna is fabricated and a close match with the simulation result is observed. Its compact form factor and low-profile nature makes it suitable for various wireless communications.

articleTitle: PUF-Secured Memory: Integrating Arbiter PUFs with Error Correction for Memory Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper presents a new method for protecting memory intellectual property by adding an Arbiter Physical Unclonable Function to the error correction application of the memory read access circuits. We use the unique features of hardware-based PUFs to create an authentication technique, which ensures that the memory IP cannot be copied to different hardware. The PUF is integrated into the error correction circuit, serving both security purposes and its main function. The PUF generates a unique signature for the read operation to validate the hardware. If the circuit is copied on different hardware, the PUF authentication fails and the copied PUF generates fake data, making the copied IP inaccessible. We ensured that the adapted error correction circuit provides no reduced effect for any correct operation. The model of the integrated PUF-based error correction circuit, its security evaluation, performance analysis are presented in the paper. Our contribution to security is in offering a practicable method for protecting memory IP, which is vital since hardware piracy is becoming an increasing issue in the semiconductor industry.

articleTitle: A Novel Structure of on-chip Multilayered Half-Turn Inductor for RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: High quality factor inductor is the prime requirement of any RFIC design. The architecture proposed in this paper is multi-layered half-Turn on-chip inductor. To improve the Q factor and performance of the on-chip inductor each metal segment of the inductor is divided in to two halves and placed innovatively into two different layers. The proposed technique used to reduce the effective parasitic capacitance and current crowding effect to improves the quality factor. The simulation results show improvement of 23.12% in quality factor and 18.94% in inductance compared to conventional stacked inductor by keeping the same area of 60µm x 60µm. The proposed inductor is implemented and simulated by using EM simulation software SONNET for obtaining Q factor and Inductance. The Proposed inductor design can work up to 5.5 GHz frequency range and suitable for high frequency RF applications

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Defective Parts from the Chicken Body Through Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Large-scale chicken and products production is one of the major sources for economic developments. Chicken behavior is a common indicator of their health conditions. Sometimes it was suffered for various reasons like transmission of farms, fighting with other chickens, and, by birth defective parts of the body. Identification of these defectives in as soon as possible to avoid the severe injury or losses. In this proposed work used image processing and supervised machine learning networks to identify these conditions with their color and texture features. Where the K-means clustering algorithm and Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix algorithms are used for feature extraction and the Fine-K-Nearest Neighbour classification model is used to classify the defective beak, comb, eye, leg, and, wounded parts of the chicken body. Defective chicken parts classification works in the proposed network achieved 98.5% of classification accuracy with 98.4%, 98.2%, and, 99.4% of sensitivity, specificity, and recall respectively.

articleTitle: A Modified Elliptical-Ring Shaped Slot Antenna for 5G-FR2 Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This investigation presents a perturbed elliptical-ring shaped slot antenna for 5G FR2 band operation. The overall compact dimension of microstrip fed antenna is 10mm×10mm×0.5mm and is structured on RT Duroid substrate. The slot width in the ground plane is varied to get the desired radiation band of 6.58 GHz at 37.5 GHzwith return loss of −35.13 dB. Also the variation in the physical dimension of radiating patch is done for enhancement of desired result.

articleTitle: A Detailed Analysis of Secrecy and Performance Metrics in Hybrid RF/ FSO Communication Systems: Implications of Composite Weibull and Log-normal Fading with M Turbulent Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In this paper, we have analyzed the secrecy performance and system operation performance for hybrid RF/FSO systems against composite Weibull-log-normal fading channel with M turbulent channels. The performance is evaluated by carrying out extensive simulations to calculate Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Bit Error Rate (BER) and outage probability, we also re-evaluate channel capacity and secrecy capacity with respect of environmental conditions. Compared with RF only system, FSO only standalone scheme and some meaningful orthogonal-modulation multicarrier IM/DD-based schemes proposed by the literatures. Similarly, the utilization of adaptive modulation schemes improved resistance to fading and roughness in systems. The above results confirm the hybridization of both RF and FSO a comprehensive solution for dependable communication in different and even hostile surrounding conditions which set this work as reliable foundation point towards forthcoming research activity or application relevance within all range telecommunication sector.

articleTitle: Design of Compact 4×4 MIMO Antenna for High-Speed Connectivity in the X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: 4×4 Multiple-input Multiple-output (MIMO) element antenna system operating at 8.56 GHz is designed and simulated in this research. Utilizing FR4 as the substrate material with a width of 0.8 mm and a size of 38×38 mm, the antenna design focuses on achieving high performance within compact form factors. The HFSS (High-Frequency Structure Simulator) software is employed for simulation studies, allowing thorough analysis of radiation patterns, impedance matching, and efficiency. Through careful optimization, the system aims to maximize spectral efficiency and reliability against multipath fading. The project explores potential applications of the MIMO antenna system in high-frequency communication scenarios such as 5G networks, satellite communication, and radar systems. Overall, this project contributes to the advancement of wireless communication technologies by offering insights into MIMO antenna design principles and optimization strategies, with the potential to enable high-speed data transmission and improved coverage in diverse deployment scenarios. Results from this study will help improve wireless communication technologies by providing a thorough knowledge of the principles and optimization methodologies for MIMO antenna design. Enhanced coverage, dependable connectivity in a variety of deployment circumstances, and lightning-fast data transfer are just a few ways in which the suggested MIMO antenna technology can shake up wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Non-Linear System Identification Using Meta-Learning Based Functional Link Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The paper describes the development of a novel nonlinear adaptive filter that integrates the principles of meta-learning into functional link networks (FLN s), which are a type of neural network used for nonlinear filtering tasks. Traditionally, nonlinear adaptive filters employ iterative optimization techniques like recursive least squares or least-mean squares, which can be complex to develop and require domain expertise for refinement. the proposed approach leverages self-supervision to learn online iterative update rules, framing the creation of FLNs as a meta-learning challenge within deep learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the new nonlinear adaptive filters achieve a 3–5 dB improvement in modeling accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A Reversible Data Hiding Scheme for ECG Signals Using CNN-PEE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The security of biomedical signals is the highest priority of any medical or clinical setup. The electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are very crucial in assessing heart health and their security is of utmost importance. A reversible data hiding scheme based on prediction error expansion (PEE) has been proposed in this work. The patient's personal data acts as a watermark and is embedded in the ECG signal. A 1D CNN based predictor has been used to obtain the sample predictions. The signals obtained from the MIT-BIH arrhythmia dataset have been utilized for training and testing the CNN model. The CNN-based predictor ensures superior performance and a high value of performance parameters.

articleTitle: Financial Forecasting with BO-RL-GAN: A Dual Approach Combining Bayesian and Reinforcement Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This work proposes a new framework, BO-RL-GAN, which encapsulates the integration of Bayesian Optimization (BO) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) within the GAN structure designed for stock market prediction. Traditional approaches can be problematic, as they are associated with the inherent randomness or pro-nature of financial information inputs. To overcome these challenges, the BO-RL-GAN introduces two approaches: first, the hyperparameters of GANs are optimized properly; second, the training strategies of GAN s are adjusted appropriately by using reinforcement learning. The validity of the suggested model was analyzed with the help of historical data from the S&P 500, NASDAQ, and FTSE 100 indexes over ten years. This was measured by Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Directional Accuracy. The BO-RL-GAN achieved an RMSE of 0.068, better than the typical GAN (0.085), LSTM-based RNN (0.079), and ARIMA (0.091), and thus showed enhanced values of predicting outlook. Similarly it, the model had the lowest MAE equal to 0.053, while it was 0.067 for the standard GAN, 0.061 for the LSTM-based RNN and 0.070 for ARIMA, proving the ability of the model to minimize the errors of predictions. Furthermore, the BO-RL-GAN has a Directional accuracy of 78%, which is higher compared to classic GAN with 65%, and LSTM-based RNN with 70% so, proving that the concept of the BO-RL-GAN is effective in capturing the market trends. These findings assert the strength of the system, as occupied in this study, in terms of the appropriateness of the presented framework as a forecasted financial instrument.

articleTitle: Optimizing Job Matching Through Automated Resume Screening with NLP and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Resume screening determines a candidate's qual-ification for a position based on their education, experience, and other resume information. Candidates are only called for interviews if their resume matches the job description. Manual resume examination is time-consuming and burdensome, prompting companies to use applicant tracking systems to shortlist candidates based on their skills. The primary cause of rejection is often a mismatch between the job role and the applicant's skill set. Job seekers must understand which job categories align with their skill sets. This study employs natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques to evaluate applicants in real time. Methods such as tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, TF-IDF, and string matching are used to identify keywords. Subsequently, ML models are applied to determine the most suitable role for each applicant. Four models-SVM, logistic regression, random forest, and k-nearest neighbors-are compared for accurate classification, with SVM outperforming the other benchmarks. This project aims to revolutionize the resume screening process by integrating advanced technologies and refining our methodologies.

articleTitle: NFPCA-LDC: A Novel Feature Pyramid with Channel Attention-Based Lung Disease Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Medical image classification requires an efficient fusion of local and global multi scale features. Convolutional kernel has receptive field of fixed size which possesses challenges to capture global features from images. The detection and classification of lung diseases from X-ray and CT images can be challenging, as different imaging modalities may offer differing degrees of clarity and resolution. These disparities in medical images provide a serious challenge to the investigation of medical images. A novel feature pyramid with channel attention-based lung disease classification (NFPCA-LDC) model is presented to address these problems. Three different datasets i.e. IQ-OTH/NCCD for lung cancer, TB_Chest_Radiography_database for Tuberculosis, and iCTCF for Covid-19 classification are used to evaluate the performance of proposed model. The results with an accuracy of 99.09 % for lung cancer, 99.59 % for tuberculosis, and 99.52 % for Covid-19 detection show the supremacy of the proposed model over existing studies.

articleTitle: Automated Power-Precision Grasp Recognition from sEMG: A Multivariate Signal Decomposition-based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Grasp recognition through surface electromyogra-phy (sEMG) has emerged as a significant element in the fields of automated control systems, human-computer interfaces, rehabil-itation systems, virtual environments, and related applications. Grasps can be categorized into different types based on their origination and force level. In power grasps, the object and hand have a rigid relationship, necessitating that all object movements originate from the arm. In contrast, precision handling enables the hand to perform intrinsic movements on the object with-out requiring arm movement. This necessitates development of methodology for recognizing these grasps from sEM G signals. This paper proposes a novel method for automated power-precision grasp recognition from sEMG. Overlapped windowing is utilized for sEMG signal segmentation. Each window frame is decomposed into its constituent modes using simplified successive multivariate variational mode decomposition (SSMVMD). Time domain features are then extracted from each mode for classification process. The KNN classifier has been utilized for binary (power and precision) and 14-class classification for NinaPro-DB4 dataset. The average subject-wise binary classification accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 89.98%, 90.51 %, 89.30%, and 89.87 %, respectively are obtained. The cross-subject binary classification accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score of 88.75 %, 89.78%, 87.40%, and 88.57%, respectively are achieved. The average subject-wise 14-class classification accuracy of 77.62% has been obtained. Further, the accuracy of 75.95% has been achieved for cross-subject 14-class classification.

Author Keywords: simplified successive multivariate variational mode decomposition (SSMVMD)

articleTitle: Blood Pressure Prediction Analysis from Doppler Ultrasound Signals Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Blood Pressure is an important diagnostic in field of medical science and sometimes BP measurement which rely on external pressure, can be unsuitable for patients with burns, mus-cle sensitivity. This study presents a low complexity (CNN based) contactless method for estimating systolic and diastolic blood pressure using Doppler ultrasound US samples from patients' blood flow. Each participant provided three Ultrasound (US) files, which were analyzed to capture blood flow patterns associated with varying blood pressures. Employing signal processing and convolutional neural networks, features from these US signals were extracted to predict blood pressure values. Initial results demonstrate the potential of this technique to offer accurate, non-pressure continuous blood pressure monitoring, enhancing diagnostics and real-time health management.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Powered Federated Learning: A Secure and Decentralized Approach to Distributed AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Integrating both federated learning and blockchain technology proposed a writing solution to the inescapable challenges of data privacy, security, and trust in FL-based decentralized machine learning environments. This paper proposes a BEFL framework with a blockchain network to ensure the trustworthiness and accountability of federated learning. The results presented in the experimental evaluation, conducted on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and a healthcare dataset, demonstrate the superiority of BEFL over FL. The BEFL framework achieved 98.5% on MNIST, CIFAR-10 82.3%, and the healthcare dataset 87.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> while surpassing standard FL by 3% on average. Regarding the convergence speed, the proposed BEFL reached the target accuracy level in 40 communication cycles for MNIST and 100 rounds for CIFAR-10, while the standard FL was 60 and 140 rounds, respectively, which is approximately 30% faster. While BEFL has a higher communication cost (180 MB for MNIST and 300 MB for CIFAR- 10) than the standard FL (150 MB and 250 MB, respectively), the authors consider it a worthy tradeoff with benefits in terms of security and transparency. The above results under adversary scenarios showed that, as with FL, the proposed BEFL framework was more robust to data poisoning, with the accuracy drop to a mere 1.5% as opposed to 5.2% of FL and a model inversion attack reconstruction accuracy of only 20% as compared to 60% of FL. The above outcomes show that through BEFL, it is possible to support distributed learning while maintaining the security of the fields of study, such as health and finance, as illustrated above.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Design of Higher-Order Efficient Wallace Tree Approximate Multipliers with Innovative Compressors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Multipliers are essential design elements in Digital Signal Processing (DSP) but their traditional design consumes a lot of power, area, and time. Approximate computing provides an alternative, particularly in multimedia applications where exact precision is not always necessary. Researchers have explored approximate multipliers to reduce resource usage while maintaining reasonable accuracy. However, there's a need to further optimize resource efficiency without compromising accuracy. It is also crucial to explore how to integrate approximate computing techniques with new architectures. This paper introduces a novel technique for designing approximate multipliers using 5:2 and 4:2 compressors. The approach uses exact compressors for the higher-order bits and approximate compressors for the lower order bits to break down partial products. This hybrid approach aims to improve computational efficiency and reduce resource usage in DSP applications. The study also investigates recursive design methods that combine lower-order multipliers to design higher-order multipliers for enhancing energy efficiency and area utilization. A 4x4 multiplier is designed using innovative compressors, and an 8x8 multiplier is constructed using the proposed 4x4 multipliers in a hierarchical manner. The research conducts thorough simulations to test and analyze the proposed approach. The proposed designs show notable improvements compared to the closest existing systems, with a 16.77% reduction in MRED, an 8.56% reduction in NMED, a 12.82% reduction in delay, an 8.46% reduction in area, and a 21.42 % decrease in power consumption.

articleTitle: Detection of Aircraft from SAR Images Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: SAR (synthetic aperture radar) images provide valuable data for detection in the field of remote sensing. Detecting aircrafts from SAR images plays a prominent role in military security and surveillance purpose in today's life. Existing methods for object detection such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Resina-Net had difficulties in detecting small aircrafts. Deep neural networks provide a prominent and efficient solution for this problem. Also, detection of objects from satellite images is a bit difficult when compared to optical images, as the SAR images generally produces only the outline of the object based on the roughness of the surface the radar waves hitting, this decreases the consideration of the features like colour etc. To detect the aircrafts from SAR images an enhanced model of YOLOv8 is proposed in this paper. This model is validated on SADD dataset and produced an accuracy of 95.3% and false alarm rate of 5.9% specifying that the model works well in different weather conditions and contains faster predictions.

articleTitle: Stabilization Through Contraction Based Output Feedback Control for a Class of Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper explores output feedback control strategies for stabilizing a particular category of nonlinear systems. Utilizing tools grounded in contraction theory, this approach offers a streamlined method to achieve stabilization of the targeted category of nonlinear systems. Certain assumptions are imposed on the associated nonlinearity of the systems to attain simple output feedback based control function. The methodology involves segmenting system dynamics into measurable and un-measurable states. A Suitable virtual system for the actual system is considered afterwards, which is stabilized with developed conteoller to ensure exponential stabilization of actual system states. Stabilization criteria are articulated in terms of controller gains. The approach is further extended to address stabilization under parametric uncertainties. Additionally, systematic adaptation laws for parameter estimation and stabilization are developed and discussed in detail. The efficacy of the developed stabilization scheme using output feedback is successfully validated using computational simulations.

articleTitle: Symptoms-Based Disease Prediction and Drug Recommendation using Hybrid Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Nowadays, medical databases are one of the largest undiscovered and underutilized databases. Every year, hospi-tals produce massive amounts of data. It is very difficult to extract knowledge from diagnosis case data. Sometimes, we ignore symptoms, which become the cause of death. Early and accurate disease prediction can benefit people and save lots of time. This paper presents a comprehensive approach to symptoms-based disease prediction and drug recommendation for people struggling with their health and medical diagnoses. This model uses machine learning classification algorithms like support vector, random forest, gradient boosting, and K nearest neighbour to make accurate predictions and recommendations. This research contributes to advancing proactive healthcare interventions, offering a potential solution to the challenges posed by resource shortages and the growing demand for medical expertise. Simulation results have shown the efficacy of the model in terms of recall, F1-score, accuracy, precision, and error.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of FinFET Based 12T SRAM Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Power optimization has become increasingly critical in the VLSI industry due to the rising density of memory systems, which leads to higher power consumption. Static RAM (SRAM) cells are particularly affected by this issue. A significant contributor to power consumption is the leakage current in transistors. Therefore, decreasing power consumption in each memory cell is essential. This paper focuses on optimizing the power of various 12T SRAM cells through an analysis of the transistor stacking technique. Instead of relying a single larger transistor, two smaller transistors are connected in series and switched off together. This configuration reduces leakage current, thereby decreasing power consumption in SRAM cells. The power usage of SRAM cells in presence and absence of the stacking method, is evaluated under different voltage conditions and performed simulations in Cadence Virtuoso.

articleTitle: YOLOv9 in Action: A Futuristic Approach to Real-Time License Plate Recognition and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The automated recognition and identification of license plates is an essential element of intelligent transportation systems that enable effective traffic management, security measures, and the development of efficient e-payment algorithms in toll booths and parking facilities. Even though license plate recognition (LPR) technology is fairly advanced, significant efforts are being made to enhance its accuracy and resilience The growing adoption of deep learning technologies across multiple industry domains, particularly computer vision, presents a novel idea implemented in this paper. To develop an approach to improve detection accuracy using YOLOv9 and transfer learning. Through combining the power of YOLOv9 with transfer learning, it is feasible to tackle the traditional LPR system's inherent flaws. Character recognition, picture pre-processing, license plate extraction, and character segmentation are the four main parts of the proposed system. Each step involves unique methodologies, primarily focusing on character recognition methodologies using YOLOv9 which has not been adequately tackled in existing research. By thorough testing and analysis, this study seeks to further the current developments in LPR systems, ensuring discernibly better-established intelligent transportation solutions. We have achieved a mAP50 Score of 99.5% and a mAP50-95 score of 71 %

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Intellectual Disability Based on Functional Connectivity Using EEG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Intellectual disability disorder (IDD) is a kind of neurodevelopmental disorder that adversely affects an individual's quality of life. Discriminating normal brain patterns from abnormal conditions is possible by identifying distinct connectivity patterns between groups. For this, Electroencephalography (EEG) is the most suitable choice in terms of the patient's ease and temporal characteristics. In this research, an automatic detection algorithm using EEG-based functional connectivity to distinguish between normal and IDD subjects IDD is proposed. This research utilized resting state EEG data gathered from 14 subjects (7 normal and 7 IDD). The methodology adopted includes alpha band extraction from the pre-processed EEG signals, followed by the computation of correlation coefficients for each non-overlapping 1-second window (epoch) to create a functional connectivity graph for both normal and IDD subjects. The connectivity features, so obtained, are then used to train multiple machine learning classifiers. After thorough evaluation, we selected the fine tree classifier due to its superior performance over other classification techniques. The generalized classification performance is obtained using Leave-One-Subject-Out Cross Validation, by leaving one subject out from each class during training. Notably, the achieved mean accuracy of 99.6% underscores the potential impact of this work in early diagnosis and personalized interventions for IDD.

articleTitle: Agri Bot a Smart Agricultural Robot for Smart Irrigation and Leaf Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper presents Agri Bot, a clever automated framework intended to help farmers in overseeing crop well being and water systems. The framework coordinates controller, plant infection discovery, soil dampness detection, and a robotized water siphoning instrument. Agri Bot uses artificial intelligence and ongoing information assortment to improve water use, upgrade crop well being, and diminish work costs. The model was tried on a small farm, bringing about a 30% decrease in water utilization and a 92% precision in early plant sickness identification. The framework's capability to further develop supportability in farming is huge, making it an important resource for small to medium-sized farms.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Binary Image Encryption Strategy Integrating Phase Shifted Holography, Fourier Transform, and Arnold Cat Map
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This work presents a hybrid binary image encryption strategy using virtual optics, phase shifted holography, Fourier transform based spectral conversion, and Arnold Cat Map based key hiding. The confidential information needed to be sent was converted to a binary image and encrypted using Mach-Zehnder configuration of phase shifted virtual holography, followed by Fourier based spectral conversion. Decryption was performed to recover the phase information from the frequency response of the deformed hologram. Towards this, all the fringe patterns had gone through inverse Fourier transform. Next, four step phase shifting algorithm was used for wrapped phase recovery, and line scan based strategy was used for unwrapping. Finally, by subtracting the reference phase map from unwrapped object phasemap, binary image was recovered. For transmitting the keys securely, Arnold Cat Map based scrambling was used. The simulation results conclusively establish the efficiency of the proposed strategy and safety against hack attacks. To analyze the overall information loss, mean square error was calculated.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Hand Gesture Classifiers Using EMG Signal and STFT-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Electromyogram (EMG) signals are used to detect different hand gestures of a person. In this study, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based feature extraction-based method is used, by which features of processed signals are extracted using a CNN model, and the features are then classified using a Machine Learning classifier. Three-hand gestures models were developed during the study, ten, seven, and four hand gestures are used to develop three models and channel wise analysis is also performed for finding of dominant channel location. These models may be helpful in the development of a prosthetic hand for patients with upper limb disabilities or a robotic hand for industrial purposes.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-RF Model for the Detection and Classification of Parkinson's Disease: Integrating Neuroimaging and Clinical Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Proper identification and differentiation of PD at a primary stage can help improve the management and enhance the general status of the patients. In this work, we present a new approach that combines the assessment of CNN deep learning models and RF in diagnosing PD based on neuroimages and clinical information. CNN provides feature extraction capability, while RF provides classification capacity, and the model combines these two characteristics, leading to high diagnostic performance. The proposed approach is then evaluated on an available real dataset, which includes MRI images and other clinical features like motor UPDRS scores, cognitive test results, age, and gender, and the experimental outcomes are reported. Based on the authors' experimental findings, the hybrid CNN-RF model produced the highest accuracy of 93 %. 7% outperforming CNN and RF standalone models with accuracies of 88. 4% and 85. The model also erected a high sensitivity of 94. 2 % and a specificity of 92. 8% provided a reliable model for differentiating PD cases and the control group. The first metric is ROC with the Area Under the Curve (AUC) of0. 96, hence adding to the confirmation of the workability of the model when discriminating between the classes. The assessments of motor UPDRS scores suggested that they were essential predictors of PD and that specific brain regions revealed by the CNN were also important indicators of PD. Although the model can achieve high accuracy, this paper has shown the limitations of relying on labelled data. Therefore, it is suggested that future work may consider utilizing semi-supervised learning.

articleTitle: Enhanced BiLSTM for Traffic Police Gesture Recognition in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: While human drivers intuitively respond to the gestures of traffic officers, autonomous vehicles do not inherently possess this capability, necessitating the development of sophisticated road traffic control gesture recognition systems. Recognizing gestures is crucial for the seamless integration of autonomous vehicles into human environments. Present-day approaches generally integrate various modalities, including bone vectors, keypoints, and picture characteristics. On the other hand, our neural network architecture uses only body skeleton data to generate state-of-the-art outcomes. We use an improved Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) model that has been carefully optimized for best results. We extensively train and assess our model on the TCG dataset-which was created especially for real-world applications-using 3D body positions across time. This method demonstrates significant advancements, improving accuracy by over 5% compared to prior models, underscoring the robust potential of our gesture recognition system for autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Integrating Enhanced Optimization Techniques with Lightweight Cryptographic Algorithms for Robust Attack Detection and Data Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: IoT devices have seen an increase recently, many of which are resource constrained and capable to provide vulnerabilities that could be exploited through a wide range of cyberattacks. Sandboxing is one way in order for the system security level to become more effective with respect how it can handle specific threats as well reduce its response time where traditional complex antimalware chain reaction signatures speed was never that solid giving new ground literals on quick granular boastful approach when performing proper access control. Therefore, this work introduces an integrated Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm with Lightweight Homomorphic Cryptography based approach to improve attack detection capability and data security for Data Stores in IoT enabled environments. A PSO algorithm is used to iterate over the Hyper-parameters in Hybrid Convolutional Autoencoder for Real-Time Network Attack Detection. Our experimental results indeed show a considerable elevation in the detection accuracy across different types of attacks including DDoS, Man-in-the-Middle, Data Exfiltration and Brute Force attacks. The detection average of the optimized HCAE model is 98.5% and for DDoS attack 99.7% was registered, being this attacked classified in highest accurate one detected by our proposal seen at Table (3). This is an increase of 7.4–12 % compared to pre-optimization adversarial accuracy for various attack types [68]. It reduces the false positive rate to 1.2%, so It increases reliability of Detection system also. According to computational efficiency, the system shows that the CPU usage drops from 75% to 55%, Memory from Drops out of memory too(i.e.80MB - >65MB) The reduction in detection latency is 37% which changes from a set of 150ms to only about 95ms, so it enables the live deployment along with real-time. The LHC scheme is equally vital for protecting data from resource-limited IoT devices, and provides an intrinsic overhead to the processing of data that tends toward zero with encryption/decryption operations taking on average only 5ms. All while able to scale up with data size up so that it's actually useful at real IoT large and medium-size deployments. We also validate the adaptability of our system to changes in network topology and new devices or removal. Comparing the results, we can observe that accuracy in one class detection remains relatively constant over time with some variation reflecting the reflective of dynamicity of IoT environments. Its detection rate is higher than signature-based intrusion de- tection systems and conventional cryptographic methods with a lower false positive rate, in addition to being computationally efficient which renders it suitable for IoT security.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis on Apodized Chirped Fiber Bragg Grating for Estimating Temperature-Strain Effects Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: An apodized Chirped Fiber Bragg Grating (CFBG) is implemented to compute the sensing response for different temperature spans together with the strain for several chirping rates. The functionality of the CFBG can be diminished in view of the introduction of broad-span of side lobes ranges. The incorporation of apodization method is largely influential to improve the sensitivity proficiency through diminishing the scale of side lobes by gradually moderating the proportions of grating index amplitude onwards the extent of grating. The sensitivity outcome of presented apodized CFBG having distinct chirping rates are appraises for several scales of uniform impact of temperature (30°C-80°C) and strain (300 μ-550 μ∊). Different Machine Learning (ML) models are implemented for predictive execution of wavelength changes in accordance with the influences of physical parameters for improving the usefulness of the sensor response in complex circumstances. This perspective is most useful regarding evaluating the structural durability of civil infrastructure as it ensures the stability, and effectiveness of CFBG-based sensitivity performance.

articleTitle: Automatic Early Detection of Potato Blight Disease Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Effective disease control in crops is essential for ensuring food security, as numerous diseases can significantly reduce agricultural productivity. Leaf disease is a crucial determinant of crop yield and quality. Potatoes are widely regarded as a vital staple in diets around the world. Potato blight, often known as late blight, is a severe disease impacting Solanaceae plants, particularly the potato. The oomycete Phytophthora infestans serves as the causal agent, posing a significant threat to potato crops by reducing yields and leading to financial losses. Identifying potato diseases is essential for ensuring food security and minimizing economic losses in agriculture. Numerous studies have explored the applications of machine learning and deep learning technologies for detecting blight diseases in affected crops. The proposed methodology outlined in our study offers a promising and effective means to enhance the accuracy of potato late blight classification. Advancements in technology can significantly improve the identification and treatment of diseases. Deep learning algorithms have been effectively employed in a range of practical applications. In our investigation, convolutional neural network models are used to analyze images of leaves. The primary aim of this initiative is to gain insights into and enhance the capacity to recognize diseases in their early phases. After the input images undergo preprocessing, the target region is distinctly isolated. CNN examines images to identify unique features, including edges, colours, and textures. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the proposed model through a diverse dataset of potato leaf images, making essential contributions to the domain of automated disease detection systems. The results of this study could enhance techniques for agricultural management and strengthen the sustainability of agriculture. This study introduces an improved CNN model designed to identify the blight disease state in potato leaf images, providing a valuable tool for farmers. The findings may aid in the evaluation and implementation of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for classifying proximal sensing images of potato plant leaves. Additional investigations could leverage this modelling framework and have the opportunity to examine various other factors to identify leaf infections at an earlier stage for crop protection.

articleTitle: A Robust Encryption Framework for Protecting Baby Monitor Videos Using XChaCha20 Algorithm with Ethereum Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: To ensure the security of baby monitor footage, it is crucial to implement a robust encryption system. Utilizing the highly efficient and secure XChaCha20 encryption method provides strong defense against potential threats, which is essential given the sensitivity of baby monitor videos. The focus should be on creating safeguards that prioritize the privacy and confidentiality of the monitored videos. The encryption system must be designed to withstand various online threats and assaults, offering a comprehensive solution for securing baby monitor footage. Additionally, incorporating blockchain technology to store the video data can further enhance security, ensuring integrity and immutability. The challenge lies in designing an encryption process that is minimally intrusive, maintaining the real-time monitoring feature without compromising security. The goal is to establish a well-thought-out XChaCha20-based encryption architecture combined with blockchain storage, ensuring robust defense while preserving the seamless functionality of baby monitors.

articleTitle: BERT-Vocal: End-to-End Voice Synthesis Enhanced with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Recent advancements in text-to-speech synthesis, pri-marily leveraging deep neural network architectures, show promising outcomes. Traditionally, models were trained on single-speaker datasets, requiring extensive retraining for new voices. However, integrating speaker embeddings with the model allows training for multi-speaker scenarios without such inten-sive retraining; however, it suffers from slower convergence. In this paper, an architecture synthesizer module embedded with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) has been developed to enhance the convergence rate. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated with Wavenet vocoders, demonstrating that BERT with attention achieves a Mean Opinion Score (MOS) of 4.2, indicating significant improvements in voice synthesis quality compared to existing models. Furthermore, a Hindi language dataset has been developed with 20 male and 20 female speakers, and our proposed model is also evaluated for this dataset.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety: Road Friction Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Road safety in India presents a multifaceted challenge due to the dynamic nature of road environments. Diverse el-ements such as vehicles, pedestrians, and livestock, considered as road friction elements, frequently disrupt traffic flow and demand efficient management. Additionally, the roads often lack clear markings or divisions, making navigation difficult for Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). To address these challenges, we propose a computer vision-based solution for detecting and classifying critical road friction elements on Indian roads. From the Indian Driving Dataset (IDD), which includes 34 annotated classes, we focus on seven main classes: animals, motorcycles, bicycles, trucks, cars, persons, and riders. Additionally, two new classes-carts and garbage-are introduced, making a total of nine classes considered as road friction elements. To locate these friction elements and enhance understanding of road environ-ments' the road label is utilized for road segmentation. The YOLOv5 model handles the detection of friction elements, while road segmentation is managed by the U-Net model. Experimental results indicate a high mAP of 0.92 for the YOLOv5 model trained on common labels and 0.89 for the model focused on less common labels. We establish ground truth by annotating images for binary classification of detected objects into friction or nonfriction elements. Using an AdaBoost classifier, we achieve 94.8 % accuracy in classifying these elements as either friction or nonfriction. This method demonstrates significant promise for advancing road safety, traffic management, and autonomous driving in India.

articleTitle: Integrating Error Level Analysis and Sensor Pattern Noise for Image Forgery Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This research integrates Sensor Pattern Noise (SPN) with Error Level Analysis (ELA) using multi-modal deep learning techniques to enhance image forgery detection. ELA is effective at detecting compression artifacts but is sensitive to subtle edits and depends heavily on image quality and compression settings. SPN complements ELA by analyzing unique camera sensor noise patterns, which are less influenced by these variables. The study employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and the Adam optimizer to improve forgery detection across datasets including CASIA 2.0, CASIA 1.0 and DSO-1, achieving significant accuracy improvements. CASIA 2.0 demonstrates a maximum accuracy of 95% with the ELA-SPN approach, highlighting robust detection capabilities enabled by feature combination. CASIA 1.0 achieves the highest performance of 86% using a voting scheme, while DSO-1 shows varied performance, reaching accuracies around 70%. This multi-modal approach leverages SPN with CNNbased deep learning to enhance detection rates and provide a reliable method for verifying digital image authenticity. By integrating SPN with CNNs, the study advances digital image forensics through effective feature fusion, overcoming limitations of traditional image-based forgery detection methods.

articleTitle: Securing Transactions Through Unmasking Credit Card Fraud Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is a pressing issue due to the increasing sophistication of fraudulent activities and the large volume of transactions processed daily. Traditional detection methods often struggle with the imbalanced nature of fraud datasets, where fraudulent transactions are rare compared to legitimate ones. This study introduces an advanced machine learning solution to address these challenges. We implemented a Random Forest algorithm enhanced with an oversampling strategy to tackle class imbalance and improve detection accuracy. The Random Forest model demonstrated exceptional performance, achieving an accuracy of 99.95%, significantly surpassing conventional methods such as Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naive Bayes and others. This high accuracy indicates the model's robustness in accurately classifying both fraudulent and legitimate transactions. The oversampling technique, which involves generating synthetic samples of the minority class, played a crucial role in enhancing the model's ability to detect fraud.

articleTitle: Vibration Analysis and Classification System for Knee Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Knee health monitoring is essential for diagnosing and preventing knee-related disorders, which are prevalent among the elderly and athletes. This paper presents a comprehensive Vibration Analysis and Classification (VAG) system that employs the GY-61 accelerometer and ESP8266 microcontroller to record knee vibrations. These vibrations are acquired and further analyzed for predicting knee condition. A machine learning framework is then used to classify the knee condition as either normal or abnormal using a pretrained model. The system integrates multiple classifiers, including Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, SVM, and Logistic Regression to ensure high accuracy and reliability. The algorithm is tested on publicly available VAG dataset and newly collected dataset for 50 subjects. The results demonstrate the system's potential for real-time knee health monitoring, providing a non-invasive and efficient solution for early diagnosis and continuous monitoring of knee conditions.

articleTitle: Prediction of Genetic Diseases using Genomic Data and XGBoost Algorithm: A High-Accuracy Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Genomic data analysis is of utmost importance in the healthcare sector as it seeks to solve the main problem of detection and genetic disease forecasting. This thesis surveys the utilization of sophisticated machine learning algorithms, specifically XGBoost, to forecast genetic diseases from genomic information. We use a database from Kaggle that focuses on genetic diseases using genomic data, providing multiple genetic markers and associated disease outcomes. In our research we focus on genetics disease prediction models using XGBoost with an efficient gradient enhancement algorithm. Through meticulous preprocessing and feature engineering, we transform raw genomic data into meaningful input features, ensuring the dataset's quality and relevance. Using the XGBoost algorithm, we build a much more efficient model that can easily detect all types of genetic disorders Our study shows an impressive accuracy of about 98%, a dataset that shows how well XGBoost performs on discovery of genetic disease patterns in the genomic. This high accuracy validation underlines the proficiency of machine learning in genomics, thus it embeds the possibility of early disease detection, personalized medicine, and targeted interventions. This research highlights the efficacy of XGBoost in genetic disease prediction and emphasizes the importance of curated datasets in advancing genomic research, contributing valuable insights to precision medicine.

articleTitle: Stock Market Prediction Using Machine Learning Based Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Many methods have been used to forecast stock market trends in the big data age, including real numbers, fuzzy time series data, fuzzy sets design, and conventional time series data. The control of semantic value data is made possible by the use of fuzzy time series data in stock market prediction, which makes accurate value predictions possible. These techniques are mostly used to forecast dynamic, non-linear datasets in a variety of industries, such as stock markets and cryptocurrencies. In order to predict stock prices, artificial intelligence (AI) methods such as neural networks (NN) have become increasingly important. Many methods have been developed to validate parametric and non-parametric theories for predicting trends and gains in the stock market using the feed-forward (FF) NN technique. A variety of soft computing techniques have been investigated in order to provide ways for decision-making based on profit and loss criteria without relying on artificial intelligence. This paper's main goal is to perform a comprehensive examination of the different prediction techniques used to estimate price and return in the stock market. The study includes a comparative review of several approaches as well as a variety of stock market forecasting strategies.

articleTitle: A Traffic-Aware Task Mapping Problem in Fog-Cloud of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (loT) is rapidly advancing, but its limited resources are often supplemented by integrating fog computing to address these constraints. Despite this, fog devices encounter challenges such as heterogeneity, widespread distribution, dynamic nature, and resource limitations. To tackle these issues, a robust task scheduling strategy is crucial for efficiently utilizing fog resources and enhancing Quality of Service (QoS). Moreover, tasks generated are dynamic in nature with disparate requirements such as deadline, cost, priority, etc. Fog resources could be utilized effectively with proper mapping of tasks based on ingress traffic on each node to meet the requirements. This research formulates the task mapping problem (TMP) with the goal of minimizing cost while improving QoS by reducing response times and deadline violations for loT tasks. It uses SVM (Support Vector Machine) to predict fog node traffic and categorizes nodes into peak-traffic and low-traffic groups. The Quantum-inspired PSO-based TM Algorithm (QPSO) has been implemented to map the tasks on these nodes. Simulation results reveal that the proposed method offers significant improvements, achieving up to 19.66% better response times, 30% cost reduction, and a 26% deadline violation rate i.e., an increase in meeting task deadlines compared to other approaches.

articleTitle: A Statistical Study of Lewy Body and Other Types of Dementia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Dementia is a global health concern, affecting over 55 million people worldwide, as reported in the Alzheimer Report 2022. It ranks 6th among chronic diseases in terms of mortality, emphasizing the need for accurate diagnosis tools. Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common type, accounting for 60-70% of cases, followed by Vascular Dementia, Lewy Body Dementia, Frontotemporal Dementia, and Parkinson's disease. Forgetfulness and loss of items are the most prevalent symptoms, occurring in 80-90% and 60-80% of cases, respectively. Machine learning techniques, such as Support Vector Machine, Gradient Boosting, and ensemble learning, have shown promise in identifying dementia stages. Deep learning techniques, including Convolutional Neural Network, Recurrent Neural Network, and Long Short-Term Memory Networks, have also been successful. Notably, Recent novel research ADCPBOBM achieved 96.64% and 98.39% accuracy for different dataset size MRI type images in the OASIS dataset and 90% accuracy for the GENFI dataset in identifying Frontotemporal Dementia. To provide more precise and useful methods for handling this expanding global health issue, more research is necessary.

articleTitle: Interview Preparation Guide Generation Leveraging GPT-4, ZSL and Hybrid Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
