abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for automating the creation of personalized interview preparation guides using GPT-4, Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL), and hybrid techniques. Our system dynamically generates tailored interview questions and preparation materials based on specific job descriptions and candidate profiles. By integrating advanced NLP with rule-based methods, it significantly enhances the relevance and quality of the content compared to traditional methods. We analyzed data from 10,000 job descriptions, 10,000 candidate profiles, and 20,000 interview questions to ensure high-quality results. The use of ZSL enables the generation of guides even for new and unfamiliar roles. Our approach achieved a 35% increase in question relevance and a 28% improvement in candidate-job matching accuracy compared to baseline methods. This research also paves the way for enhancing AI tools in HR, supporting personalized learning, performance reviews, and career planning.

articleTitle: Exploring GHOST-DF Dataset for Deep-Learning Based Deepfake Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In recent years, the quality of synthetic media has significantly improved. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based generation, editing, or style transfers are so real to be detected with the naked eye. This research covers the domain of AI -generated fake imagery, which happens when someone adopts another's identity. This transfer includes expression, emotion, hair, and makeup, but it also extends beyond these specific styles. We propose a dataset to power deep-fake forensics. The generated GHOST-DF dataset contains 97212 males and 65715 females, synthetically swapped facial images. The employed method for generation is the Generative High-fidelity One Shot Transfer (GHOST). The target dataset contains 15270 and 14731 real images of males and females extracted from CelebAMask-HQ. A state-of-the-art (SOTA) deep learning-based universal deepfake detector is used to validate the proposed dataset. On running inference, a signifi-cant drop in the performance of the employed SOTA framework, i.e., Universal Fake Detector, to 64.6% has been observed. Using transfer learning, we fine-tuned the detector model and achieved an overall performance improvement of 97.9 % for our introduced dataset. Furthermore, the fine-tuned model is tested on other fake datasets to establish its generalization ability. The project page is https:/hdthub.com/anushka0415/GHOST-DF.

articleTitle: Melspectrogram Based Music Genre Classification System Using Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In recent years, the popularity of music recommendation systems has surged, driven by the growth of diverse music content and the variety of digital music libraries accessible with a simple tap. Digital music collections are frequently organized based on genre labels, and recommendation systems rely on music genres to propose new tracks to listeners. Manually classifying a substantial music volume can be a laborious and time-consuming task. Hence, automated music classification by genre emerges as a pivotal task. Using machine learning(ML) to automatically classify music by genre offers a potentially faster and arguably more precise alternative to manual classification. Various deep-learning techniques have been employed for music classification tasks like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. This paper discusses the drawbacks of the various Deep Learning(DL) Techniques and the possible use of Vision Transformers(ViTs) in Music Classification. Although the Transformer architecture has emerged as the dominant choice for natural language processing tasks, its utilization in computer vision applications remain constrained. In essence, this paper aims to show that the Vision Transformer can be used effectively to classify music based on images, which could be an innovative approach in the field of music genre classification.

articleTitle: Hybrid Framework for Medical Image Classification: Integrating Quantum DE and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> presents an innovative hybrid framework for medical image classification, combining Quantum Differential Evolution (QDE) with deep learning techniques. Initially, wavelet and Gaussian filters are applied in the preprocessing stage to enhance image features. Otsu thresholding is then used for image segmentation to identify regions of interest. The main novelty of this approach is the integration of the Quantum Differential Evolution algorithm, an optimization technique inspired by quantum computing principles. This framework utilizes QDE's global exploration abilities to optimize key features from segmented medical images. These optimized features are subsequently input into a Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture for accurate classification. The core innovation of this approach lies in employing Quantum Differential Evolution for an efficient and adaptive optimization process, enhancing feature extraction. Experimental results highlight the effectiveness of this Quantum Differential Evolution-based framework, demonstrating improved classification accuracy and robustness. This model represents a significant advancement in medical image classification, illustrating the benefits of merging quantum-inspired optimization with deep learning. This unique hybrid methodology contributes to the progress of medical image analysis and classification systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Security for Medical Implants in Internet of Bio-Nano Things Using LSTM-Based Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Deep learning algorithms are efficient at predicting good models and a thorough understanding of similar problems to provide effective solutions more quickly. On the other hand, the Internet of Bio-Nano Things provides communication between bio-nano devices and remote healthcare centres. Usually, bio-nano devices do not implement security features due to resource constraints, violating client data governance. Such a network requires security features installed on a wearable device and reliable algorithms that can speedily assess patient data. Deep learning algorithms can improve bio-nano network security by preserving sensitive data. In this article, we discussed the resources of Implantable Medical Devices such as processor, memory and battery that are prone to Resource Depletion attacks. An implanted device's lifespan could be cut short by these attacks and data privacy will be lost. Many conventional models have provided security when the patient is not undergoing any physical activity. But, in this article, we explained how Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is utilized in analysing noisy data collected during various physical activities of the person. Our model predicts the fake device readers and achieved a mean accuracy of 99.8%.

articleTitle: Harnessing Nature's Wisdom for Resource Optimization and Load Balancing in Edge and Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: With the new advancements and rapid evolution in the loT (Internet of Things) environment and the rise in demand for low-latency applications, fog and edge computing epitome have emerged as promising solutions to meet the stringent requirements of real-time data processing and analysis. However, efficient resource utilization and load balancing are critical challenges in fog and edge computing environments due to the heterogeneous nature of devices and dynamic workloads. So, here we propose an approach for resource management and task distribution in fog and edge computing environments leveraging nature-inspired algorithm The Clonal Selection Algorithm (CLONALG). The application of this algorithm provides an ideal or near-perfect solution. In this paper, we have presented a supported and detailed comparison of this nature- inspired meta-heuristic algorithm based on numerous factors that influence how well load balancing and resource optimization work together to produce better optimal solutions.

articleTitle: High Dimensionality Reduction and Optimized Mental Health Monitoring Using Diverse Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Emotion recognition is becoming increasingly vital in fields like mental health diagnostics, interaction between humans and computers, and personalized technology. Accurately identifying emotions improves our comprehension of human behaviour and guides therapeutic interventions, making real-time detection particularly beneficial in clinical settings and user experience design. Electroencephalogram (EEG) brainwave data, which records the brain's electrical signals through non-invasive scalp sensors, serves as a powerful tool for recognizing emotions. It provides insights into the subtle neural dynamics linked to different emotional states, although effective processing and analysis still pose challenges. This study evaluates three sophisticated neural network frameworks such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), and Deep Neural Networks (DNN)-to determine their effectiveness in classifying emotional statesfrom EEG data. Both GRU and LSTM achieving a 97% accuracy in their tests. However, DNN architecture demonstrated a significant advantage, attaining an accuracy of 98.44% on the test dataset. This indicates the DNN's ability to identify complex patterns in EEG data, emphasizing its potential to enhance emotion recognition and support future developments in emotion-sensitive technologies.

articleTitle: Image Forgery Detection Using Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The growing demand for trustworthy picture forgery detection techniques to maintain the integrity of visual content across a range of applications is addressed in this work. To improve picture authentication accuracy and efficiency, a user-friendly cascaded framework combining Support Vector Machines (SVM) and VGG 16 is presented. First, a highly effective supervised learning system called Support Vector Machines (SVM) rapidly filters photos by identifying overt alteration indi-cators. After passing this phase, images are examined and refined even more with the help of the VGG 16 deep learning model. When SVM and VGG16 are combined, their complimentary strengths are utilised, which improves accuracy and speeds up identification when compared to other approaches. According to benchmark datasets, the proposed method outperforms earlier methods with respect to accuracy and computational efficiency. This strategy may benefit many real-world applications- based on forensic verification, verification of media integrity, medical image authentication, and intellectual property protection-in the here-and-now solutions. This work enhances the confidence and trustworthiness of digital communications by providing an efficient, friendly user tool for the verification of visual content.

articleTitle: SPAMNet: A Selective Pixel Attention Mapping Network for Enhanced Semantic Segmentation in Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This study proposes Selective Pixel Attention Mapping Network (SPAMNet), a novel deep learning architecture for semantic segmentation, designed to capture both local and global contextual information. By leveraging Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) combined with two advanced attention mechanisms, global sparsemax and selective attention, SPAMNet enhances segmentation precision. The architecture utilizes feature extraction networks (FXNs), such as MobileNetEdge and Xception, to gather deep features. Experimental results on a public dataset show that SPAMNet outperforms existing models in segmentation accuracy, demonstrating its effectiveness in complex image analysis tasks.

articleTitle: Collaborative Artificial Intelligence in a Public Blockchain Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Significant advancements in artificial intelligence have been made recently, thanks to machine learning, albeit these are typically rather centralized. Datasets of considerable size often remain restricted, while publicly available models swiftly lose relevance without ongoing data collection and retraining. Predictions are usually retailed on a per-query basis. Our solution enables users to create collaborative datasets and utilizes smart contracts for the perpetual hosting of an updated model. The public can freely access this model on a blockchain for inference. Games, recommender systems, personal assistants, and other situations where a model is frequently applied to comparable input are examples of ideal learning challenges. We suggest gamified incentive structures that include financial and non-financial rewards for supplying high-quality data to ensure that the model remains accurate when applied to a particular test set.

articleTitle: VidSegNet: A New Benchmark for Single Object Segmentation Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Single Object Segmentation Tracking (SOST) is a crucial task in computer vision with numerous real-world applications, such as video surveillance, sports performance evaluation, and medical analysis. Despite its importance, SOST faces several challenges, including object occlusion, interference from similar objects, and deformation. The newly created model or algorithms must be resilient to such difficult circumstances. To test this condition, a high-quality dataset is required. This paper introduces a new benchmark dataset specifically designed to address the future development of single object segmentation, focusing on real-world applications and challenges such as persis-tent tracking, occlusion, scale variation, and background clutter which contains 100 real-world videos. The dataset is trained and tested on three state-of-the-art algorithms: SiamMask, XMem, and Cuite, offering researchers essential metrics to bootstrap the advancement of their proposed methods in the field of SOST. The dataset can be found at: https://github.com/asfakalilVidSegNet.

articleTitle: Audio Classification Using Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Audio classification is essential for numerous ap-plications, including environmental sound monitoring, speech recognition systems and music genre classification. The ability to accurately classify audio data improves the functionality of these systems, leading to improved user experiences and more effective automation. Accurate audio classification can improve emergency response systems by detecting distress sounds, en-hance smart home devices with better sound recognition and advance healthcare through precise classification of respiratory sounds. Machine learning has transformed audio classification by enabling systems to automatically learn patterns in audio data, enhancing applications like speech recognition and environmental sound monitoring. Convolutional Neural Networks(CNNs), in particular, have proven highly effective for audio classification by extracting hierarchical features from audio spectrograms. This paper proposes an efficient ensemble model involving VGG16, ResNet50 and DenseNet121. The audio data are first converted to spectrograms, which are then used as inputs for the CNN models. The individual pre-trained models are modified to adapt their classifiers to the specific audio classification task, with the number of output classes determined by the dataset. The ensemble model combines the outputs from the three networks, incorporating batch normalization and dropout to improve generalization. By leveraging the complementary strengths of VGG16, ResNet50 and DenseNet121, the ensemble model shows an impressive accuracy of 97.4% on the UrbanSound8K dataset.

articleTitle: A Review for Increasing the Network Performance by Eliminating the Effect of Jamming Attack in Mobile Ad-Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: As we know Mobile Ad Hoc Network is constructed by open and shared medium. Due to this shared nature of media, attacker can easily perform malicious activity. in order to block the unauthorized node to access the network, Network administrator focus on the network security by making different policies and provisions. In this Ad Hoc network, most serious issue which is arising today is jamming attack. It must be resolved in efficient manner with increasing the network performance. Jamming is one of the types of DoS problem. Jammer (Attacker in jamming attack) is one who disturbs the ongoing data transmission between authentic nodes of these networks. Jammer prevents the authorized message to reach out at destination end it also degrades the performance of Ad Hoc Network. In the paper we have presented a detailed review study of jamming attack and there different solutions with there pros and cons. This article represent the comparative study of suitable work done on various jamming, types of jammer and there prevention schemes

articleTitle: The Role of AI and Machine Learning in the Evolution of 5G and Beyond Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This article will examine the current capabilities of 5G and B5G networks in terms of artificial intelligence and machine learning. The research delves into several applications of AI and ML within the telecom industry. Neural networks are introduced as a class of tools for decision-making and statistical data modelling that are often nonlinear. Data pattern discovery and the representation of complex connections between input and output parameters in systems are common uses for these. This class of neural networks includes recurrent, convolutional, feed-forward, and deep neural networks. When improving a system property or maximising a collective reward, reinforcement learning focuses on the behaviours that intelligent agents must do. One advantage of deep reinforcement learning is its ability to handle unstructured input. This is achieved by combining deep neural networks. We offer hybrid solutions, like expert knowledge aided machine learning and mixed analytical and machine learning models. Lastly, further targeted approaches are showcased, including GANs, unsupervised learning, and clustering. CF M-MIMO technology, which stands for cell-free massive MIMO, is the most promising idea in B5G. The appealing aspects of CF M-MIMO systems, such as power distribution and channel estimation, are with their downsides. There have been numerous successful applications of deep learning (DL) across many scientific domains, including wireless communications. According to the research by Lazaros Alexios Iliadis et al., CF M-MIMO networks use cutting-edge DL techniques. We provide the most popular DL models and review cell-free network fundamentals here. The endnotes emphasise the potential avenues for further study.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Facial Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) is a technique that uses facial expression analysis and examination to identify human emotions. It is often used to identify different human behavioural patterns and deep learning has proven to be revolutionary in performing FER. In this paper, three deep learning models, namely ResNet50, EfficientNet, and VGG16, have been used to do the same through transfer learning. A comparative analysis has been conducted between the models under consider-ation based on various performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Dataset used in this paper is CK+ (Cohn-Kanade Extended dataset), containing a collection of images of human faces showing different facial expressions. From the experimental study on the CK+ dataset, EfficientNet has outperformed the compared models with an accuracy of 98.31 %, while ResNet50 and VGG16 achieved 91.14% and 82.42 % respectively. Moreover, the loss curve indicates that EfficientNet is better in convergence.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Recognition and Classification Using Different Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Heart disease in India causes a mortality rate of around one individual each day. The heart is the most crucial organ in the human body. The heart serves two main functions: firstly, it collects blood from the body's tissues and propels it to the lungs; secondly, it collects blood from the lungs and propels it to all the tissues in the body. Cardiovascular disease has resulted in the deaths of several individuals. Accurately anticipating disease at the proper moment is essential due to this rationale. Utilizing machine learning Furthermore, diseases may be readily recognized and predicted. Additionally, it encompasses several algorithms on the Heart Disease Dataset. The dataset utilized in this study was acquired from Kaggle. The main objective of this study is to examine essential machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbours, Decision Tree Classifier, and Support Vector Machine, to predict heart disease. The Decision Tree Classifier model we obtained has achieved an accuracy score of 80.0%. The Random Forest Classifier achieved a score of 84.0%. The Support Vector Classifier achieves an accuracy of 83.0% using a linear kernel. The K-Neighbours Classifier beat all previously used approaches, attaining a maximum score of 88 % with the eight closest neighbors.

articleTitle: Obstacle-Aware Walking Stick: Enhancing Mobility for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The loss of vision dramatically impacts one's life, thus necessitating the need for more advanced navigation aids other than previously existing white canes. Our project aims to tackle this challenge by introducing an innovative ultra-sonic sensor integrated with IoT technology. This affordable, detachable, portable system can be used with any pre-existing white canes used by visually disabled people, going beyond other alternatives. Our approach consists of solid designing and testing procedures to ensure precision, adaptability, and user-friendliness. The groundwork for this project entails an exhaustive review of existing literature on assistive technology that has led to innovative approaches to addressing these needs. This engineering system uses Raspberry Pi Pico, HCSR04 Ultra-sonic Sensor, and carefully chosen components. Rigorous testing supports the functional validation, accuracy, and range of claims. Its capacity for working remarkably well, irrespective of any scenario, is demonstrated through the findings presented. Besides its technical aspects, our project looks deeper into socio-economic issues like accessibility concerns, inclusive promotion, and cost-related matters. In particular, the ethical aspects surrounding this undertaking have been examined alongside government backing and global distribution hurdles to emphasize the holistic nature of this research endeavor.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Approach to Multi-Class Classification of Vocal Disorders: Laryngocele and Vox Senilis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The classification of audio signals has been a significant challenge in machine learning, especially with regard to the early identification of voice disorders. However, traditional techniques based on raw audio feature extraction have been shown to be not as effective due to the complex and non-stationary capacities of individuals experiencing speech difficulties. Therefore, the audio information related to two vocal disorders including Laryn-gocele and Vox Senilis have been transformed into an informative representation, Mel-Spectrogram. This helps in capturing both temporal as well as spectral characteristics in a manner consistent with typical auditory perception. In this study, the standalone Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and various ensemble methods in conjection with machine learning techniques (CNN-ML) models have been explored for classification of audio signals based on Mel-Spectrogram. The CNN-Support Vector Machine (SVM) based ensemble method has excelled with accuracy of 96.23% at the extraction of hierarchical features corresponding to the Mel-Spectrograms while the SVM component provides robust classification capabilities. Overall, a relative improvement of 41.18% has been observed for CNN-SVM using Adamax optimizer when compared to the performance of ensemble techniques using Adam optimizer.

articleTitle: Advanced Design of Numerical Control Oscillators with Enhanced CORDIC Pipelining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The numerically controlled oscillator (NCO) serves as an indispensable component in digital communication systems, including Digital Radio, Modems, Digital Converters, and computer base stations. Its primary function lies in ensuring the stability of output frequency within the digital phase-locked loop (D-PLL), thereby facilitating reliable communication channels. In addition to its pivotal role within the D- PLL, the NCO holds significant importance in applications such as beamforming, where its performance directly impacts the entire system's functionality. Consequently, achieving high precision in the NCO's operational attributes becomes a central theme and a formidable challenge when optimizing the system performance. In this paper, the focus is on the pipelined CORDIC algorithm and its integration with the basic model of an NCO. An assessment is performed on the improved NCO in terms of its resource utilization and power. Furthermore, the beamforming capabilities of the improved NCO design are also investigated.

articleTitle: Development of a Haptic Exo-Suit with Tactile Feedback in Hand Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Stroke survivors with hemiplegia or paralysis often struggle with daily tasks due to impaired hand function and timely physiotherapy is essential for motor function recovery. This study presents a haptic forearm exo-suit designed to assist stroke rehabilitation by mimicking a physiotherapist's tactile feedback. The exo-suit integrates force-myography (FMG) and flexible tactile sensors to monitor muscle activity, finger movements, arm rigidity and tactile force in real-time. An AI-driven algorithm processes this sensor data to control the exo-suit's actuation system, which mimics natural finger movements and provides targeted therapeutic exercises. Initial testing demonstrated the exo-suit's effectiveness in simulating a physiothera-pist's precise and gradual actuation, improving the rehabilitation process. Evaluations on both healthy participants and those under simulated paralysis confirmed the hardware's capability and the reliability of the signal processing algorithms. Among the machine learning algorithms applied, k-nearest neighbors (KNN) achieved the highest accuracy at 86 %, with 89% precision and 84% recall. The proposed exo-suit offers an affordable and adaptive solution for individuals with partial arm paralysis, with real-time therapy adjustments that may significantly enhance recovery and improve the quality of life for stroke patients.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Real-Time Accident Detection with Smart Emergency Response System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Accidental deaths remain a significant threaten the lives of people worldwide, and recurrently cause severe injuries due to slow reportage and response. The existing methods employed to detect accidental occurrences rely on written reports or structured systems that are usually less reliable, thus slow reporting and high, false alarms rates. This paper proposes a real-time and automated accident detection system which aims at enhancing the identification process by using the deep learning YOLOv5 and YOLOv8. Using the object detection and vehicle tracking, the system can calculate the speed of vehicles and detect collision events, as well as bounding box movements with IoU (Intersection over Union) that let the system track constant collisions past defined thresholds. Contrary to traditional systems, this approach significantly reduces false positive while at the same time increasing detection accuracy. When an accident is found, the system uses geographic results from OpenStreetMap and the Haversine formula to notify the closest emergency services which include hospitals and police stations. Describing its use in real traffic proves that this scalable approach enhances both detection and response time rates. This research makes small advancements towards smarter transportation systems by improving the detection and timely alerting, thereby reducing accident death tolls by quicker responses.

articleTitle: Advanced Security Mechanism for Real-Time 5G Healthcare Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Securing smart healthcare systems is of utmost importance in the ever-changing realm of 5G communications. Existing security solutions frequently encounter challenges when safeguarding sensitive data in healthcare devices with limited resources, resulting in vulnerabilities in patient care networks. The paper presents a robust cybersecurity architecture for 5G-enabled healthcare. It employs Lightweight Cryptography (LWC) and Zero Trust Architecture to guarantee secure communication across the entire process, from device production to patient interaction. The suggested system exhibits robustness in the face of attacks such as replay, man-in-the-middle, and impersonation. Although communication costs have only increased by a modest 11%, the framework manages to decrease computing overhead by 12%, improving energy efficiency and protecting significant healthcare infrastructure.

articleTitle: Selective Privacy Control on Video Feed Using Pre-Trained DNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This article introduces an approach to provide privacy control on live video feeds using a pretrained D NN model. Due to privacy being a major concern in today's world, this approach would ensure the blurring of the faces in live feeds on a real-time basis to protect the privacy of participants. Users are also provided with the liberty to selectively blur/unblur the face of any specific participants as required, thereby providing enhanced flexibility and control over privacy settings during live video conferences or communications. The proposed approach also lets users upload a picture of someone. This ensures that the person's identity stays unobfuscated in the video stream. This feature comes in handy when some people are required to be seen, for example, in work meetings and online conferences. The developed solution can blur faces in real time and let users unblur or keep certain faces clear. This gives users a complete set of tools to handle privacy concerns. It tackles the growing concerns about facial privacy in our digital world. This solution enhances privacy during live video calls by utilizing advanced computer vision to selectively blur unwanted faces while maintaining clear visibility of intended participants.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Energy Storage System Application in Contemporary Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The contemporary power system with a growing presence of variable renewable energy sources, challenges like grid impedance, higher-frequency fluctuations, and overall reliability become increasingly essential, particularly when considering networks with 100% renewable energy as the ultimate smart grid development. In such a scenario, energy storage systems are being widely used in bulk power networks as well as microgrids, which are proving to be an invaluable tool for enabling the smooth integration of renewable energy sources. As such, they are positioned to be paramount in future renewable energy networks. To solve the issue of RES integration, this article conducts a thorough analysis of several quickly developing energy storage technologies, with an emphasis on superconducting magnetic, batteries, flywheel, and thermal energy storage. To improve grid operation, market dynamics, stability, and control, the review covers their applications within power grids and offers insights into how they evolve in microgrids, distribution networks, and transmission grids.

articleTitle: Compressed YOLOv8 Models for Efficient Human Head Detection in Transit Video Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The rapid urbanization of India has led to a surge in the use of intelligent vehicle, traffic and surveillance systems to meet the transportation needs of its growing population. Effective management of these systems necessitates automation in tracking and monitoring of passengers. This research paper addresses this issue by leveraging the YOLOv8 architectures, a state-of-the-art object detection model, as the foundation for head detection. The primary objective is to optimize this architecture for real-time head detection at the edge, ensuring minimal computational demands on a system's onboard hardware. We are able to achieve a high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mAP}_{0.5}^{\text{val}}$</tex> of 98% and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mAP}_{0.5.0.95}^{\text{val}}$</tex> of 80% for nano category of models. These provided an inference speed of 16.15 FPS on CPU devices. We utilize compression techniques on the YOLOv8 models such as Training Aware Quantization and Gradual Magnitude Pruning, balancing the tradeoff between speed and accuracy for the head detection system. This helped in accelerating the results to a massive 4x boost in inference speed of 63.45 FPS on CPU with almost similar mAP values. The complete framework is built around Indian transit data. Some of the unique challenges faced while using such data include varying lighting conditions, headwear diversity, occlusion, and crowded scenarios during peak hours, we have tried our best to incorporate such variety of data points during training of the models.

articleTitle: Novel Artificial-Intelligence Based Navigation Modelling for Unmanned Vehicular System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Unmanned Vehicular System (UVS) is the next revolutionary innovations of Intelligent Transport System powered by high-rate data transmission of 6G. The prime agenda of UVS is to offer a driver less car service from source to destination points with more emphasis over the accuracy and precision towards following the specified path. At present, such UVS is mechanized and look forward for travelling small distance traffic lanes with highly controlled environment. However, such UVS when exposed to real-time traffic system will be exposed to dynamic traffic density and only way to solve this challenge is to embed a proper decision making system within the vehicular node. Hence, Artificial Intelligence (AI) could significantly assist in doing so. Review of existing AI based mechanism towards traffic mobility and vehicular network has made couple of improvement; however, such improvements still fall very short when it comes to use AI on UVS. Therefore, the proposed study addresses this open-end challenge by developing a novel computational framework where AI is used for analysing the traffic attributes of lane system following by yielding a higher granularity in decision making for proper navigation of driver less car. An urban traffic environment is developed followed by configuring the network devices to acquire the traffic related information, which are then aggregated and forwarded to AI-based processor inside the vehicle. The outcome of the study is benchmarked with the existing schemes to find that proposed scheme offers better accuracy and safer driving experience on near-real world traffic system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Wavelet Transform on fPCG Signals for Denoising and Peak Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Fetal Phonocardiogram (fPCG) is a bio-signal obtained from recording the heart sounds from stethoscopes or auditory transducers for auscultations of FHR. Analysis of this data helps to give early diagnosis of any irregularity throughout Fetal development process. However, the analysis of this signal poses many challenges due to noise components like Motion Artifacts and Respiration of the Foetus and Mother, Uterine Contractions, Power Line Interference, Sensor Noise as well as Background Noise. Many approaches have been presented by the researchers to extract characteristic heart sound peaks from these signals to estimate the heart rate and to detect the abnormalities like arrhythmia. In this work, we present the results of application of advanced signal processing techniques such as wavelet transform with adaptive thresholding, to extract the peaks of the fPCG signal. Simulations have been performed on the set of real data from fetus as well as simulated signals available in the resources. Simulation results show that Discrete Wavelet Transform with adaptive thresholding is a better technique for denoising the signal and isolating the heartbeat peaks as compared to other studies discussed in various resources. This study also includes evaluation of various parameters employed in the processes including the verification of peaks by setting up a window of specific time to analyze the peak count within each window for consistent peak extraction results. Various combinations of wavelets with different thresholding techniques have been studied and evaluated for accuracy.

articleTitle: ZAIA: Zero-trust Authentication and Identity Attestation Framework for AI-Enabled IIoTs in Smart Manufacturing Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of B5G/6G-enabled AI-based Industrial Internet of Things (AIeIIoTs) crucial for Smart Manufacturing Industry 5.0 (SMIE), this research introduces ZAIA, a NIST-Zero Trust Architecture (NIST-ZTA)-based identity attestation and key agreement framework. Tailored for Split Learning in 6G-SMIE/ AIeIIoTs, ZAIA enhances security by integrating NIST-Principles of Least Privilege (NIST-POLP). It employs NIST-ZTA to eliminate trust assumptions between the edge-enabled Access Point (EAP) and cloud-enabled remote Authentication Server (CAS), ensuring robust cryptographic authentication. ZAIA features a resilient anonymity-preserving cryptographic framework using AES-128 in Galois-Counter Mode (GCM) and Symmetric Key Cryptography for mutual authentication, providing strong defense against various threats. Simulations and real-time testing demonstrate ZAIA's significant optimization in computational cost (12.5%) and communicational cost (14.29%), over current methods in resource-constrained 6G-AIeIIoTs. Formal and informal security analyses, including Scyther-Formal Security Analysis Tool, further validate ZAIA's robust security in the 6G-AIeIIoTs environment.

articleTitle: Trusted Customized Blockchain-Enabled Vaccine Distribution Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In order to overcome the shortcomings of conventional vaccine distribution systems, this study presents a unique Trusted Customized Blockchain-Enabled Vaccine Distribution Framework. The framework, built using a custom blockchain developed with Golang, offers a secure, transparent, and efficient supply chain. It leverages blockchain's immutability to ensure data integrity and track vaccine movement (batch ID, manufacturer, distribution date). Smart contracts automate transactions and enhance security. Performance analysis demonstrates the framework's scalability and efficiency in handling increasing transaction volumes. The outcome demonstrates that the goal of this strategy has the ability to transform vaccination distribution and promote a more reliable and robust international system.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning for the Identification and Categorization of Fruit Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The precise assessment of fruit quality and the detection of illnesses are critical tasks in the agriculture sector. One important component that has a direct impact on consumers' physical well-being and inclination to buy is the freshness of fruits and vegetables. Analyzing the degree of freshness in fruits and vegetables is important since it has a big impact on how market prices are set. Fruit and vegetable classification and identification by machine vision is difficult because of their comparable colors, textures, and external environmental elements including illumination, reflections, and complicated backdrops. This study presents a comprehensive overview of methods for detecting and classifying the quality of fruits and plants using several strategies for feature extraction and classification. Several academics have suggested various ways including binarization, histogram-based approaches, Gray Level Co-occurrence matrix, machine learning techniques, and deep learning. The outcome of our study showcases the results obtained from different methodologies, together with their respective benefits and challenges. In conclusion, we will discuss potential areas for improvement and future directions for additional research.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of High Speed Self-Biased DTDC for Flash ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: To maximize speed and power economy, the requirement for high speed low power analogue to digital converters (ADC's) is driving towards the adoption of dynamic double tail comparator. The comparator is one of most power hungry block of analog to digital converter and it also directly affects the ADC's overall performance. It is possible to switch on the comparator just when it is required to limit the power usage of ADC. Because of their power economy and great speed, many high speed and low power ADCs employ regenerative comparators. Therefore, a unique self-biased double tail dynamic comparator (DTDC) is developed to improve latch regeneration performance, hence reducing overall latency and enabling use in more hustle flash ADCs. Using GPDK 45nm technology, the suggested comparator is built and simulated in Cadence® Virtuoso Analogue Design Environment. The circuits are tested using a 1.0 Volt DC supply voltage and a clock frequency of 200MHz.

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Signal Control System Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Traffic congestion remains a major issue in urban areas, leading to environmental deterioration through increased noise and air pollution. Existing traffic management solutions often fall short in adapting to the dynamic nature of urban traffic patterns. Adaptive traffic control systems utilizing Reinforcement Learning (RL) offer a promising alternative by adjusting traffic signals based on real-time traffic conditions in each lane to alleviate congestion. In this paper, we propose an RL-based approach leveraging Deep Q-Networks (DQN) to minimize the cumulative waiting time of vehicles at intersections. Our method involves training a deep neural network to predict Q-values for various traffic signal actions, which are then used to optimize traffic light changes. The simulation environment is set up using SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility) for network and traffic generation, with TraCI (Traffic Control Interface) providing real-time traffic data. Our approach demonstrates significant improvements over the traditional methods. Additionally, we include visualizations of the simulation results to illustrate the effectiveness of our RL-based traffic control system.

articleTitle: STAR-RIS Assisted Overlay Cognitive Radio Network Using DRL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Simul-taneously Transmitting and Reflecting Reconfigurable Intelli-gent Surfaces (STAR-RIS) in overlay Cognitive Radio Network (CRN) to enhance communication efficiency and reliability. We focus on using the Rate Split Multiple Access (RSMA) scheme over Nakagami-m fading channels to optimize spectrum usage and maximize sum rate while maintaining practicality and ur-ban environmental constraints. We employ Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques, mainly the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithms, to maximize the sum rate for all users while ensuring Quality of Service (QoS) and primary user cooperation. Our simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in network performance, highlighting the potency of our proposed solution in urban environments. The findings underscore the potential of integrating STAR-RIS and RSMA to advance the capabilities of future wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: The Impact of Cloud Computing on Construction Practices in Nepal: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Cloud computing has emerged as a transformative technology with significant potential for various industries, including the construction sector. This research paper explores its role in the construction industry and its impact on proj ect management, collaboration, data storage, and security. Through an in-depth analysis of existing literature, case studies, and industry practices, the paper highlights the benefits, challenges, and future prospects of cloud computing adoption in construction. The findings aim to help industry professionals and policymakers understand the potential of cloud computing and make informed decisions regarding its implementation in construction projects. Additionally, this research examines the implementation of cloud computing in Nepal's construction industry and its impact on sustainable projects. It combines existing research findings with a survey conducted among 58 construction companies to identify key factors contributing to successful adoption. A Relative Importance Index (RII) is utilized to determine the relative importance of these factors, providing insights into the specific context of cloud computing adoption in Nepal's construction sector.

articleTitle: Aspect Category Detection with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Aspect Category Detection (ACD), a sub-task of Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA), has become prominent in recent years due to the rise in customer reviews. Unlike conventional ABSA research that deals with domains such as laptops and restaurants, our research take a novel approach by analyzing three datasets associated to Indian government policies, Indian Budget and Parliamentary debates. We explore various methods for aspect category detection, dividing them into supervised and unsupervised learning categories, ultimately identifying the most suitable approach for our research. We began by presenting the new Topic-Attention Network Model (TANM) that employs the Swish activation function to increase the precision and reliability of aspect category recognition. The proposed model adapts contextual word embedding with topic distribution, which uses Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) to infer aspect categories from the text. The topic-aware attention mechanism is another facet of our approach since it focus on those words which could be important for each aspect. The outcome of the context vectors is then passed through a fully connected layer for accurate aspect category prediction. Thus the method significantly contributes positive improvement in aspect-based sentiment analysis by showing enhanced capability in pinpointing subtle and implicit facets.

articleTitle: UX-Net Based Speech Separation Scheme using Parameterized Hypercomplex Convolutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This paper presents a modified U-Net-based approach for speech separation that employs parameterized hy-percomplex convolutions. The proposed model is capable of handling both single and multi-microphone input signals. It is for signals in both the frequency and time domains, and then utilizes a separation module to estimate the masks of the speech sources. The UX block filters the input across different resolutions to approximate these masks. The overall number of model parameters is reduced by leveraging the properties of Clifford algebra. Kronecker products are utilized for the parameterization of the hypercomplex convolution layers. The parameterized hypercomplex networks are able to subsume the algebraic rules from the data, thus enabling their application across domains ranging from I-D to n-D. Consequently, the number of network parameters can be reduced to l/n using these PHC layers, where n is a hyperparameter indicating the hypercomplex domain.

articleTitle: Children's Speech Emotion Recognition Using Feature Fusion-Based Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This study introduces the C-BESD (Children Bilin-gual Emotion Speech Dataset), a novel and comprehensive dataset. It is collected from children aged 6–12 years and captures common emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, disgust, neutrality, and fear. The C- BESD dataset is distinguished by its inclusion of bilingual speech samples, enhancing its applicability across diverse linguistic contexts. This dataset aims to provide the speech research community with a robust resource specifically tailored for children's speech emotion recognition (SER). Utilizing the C-BESB dataset, a preliminary SER system was developed employing traditional feature extraction methods such as mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC), zero crossing rate (ZCR), harmonic ratio, and pitch. These features were used to train a convolution neural network (CNN), which achieved an accuracy of 76%, demonstrating the dataset's potential effectiveness. The primary contribution of this work is the creation and introduction of a generalized and robust SER dataset specifically for children. The results showcase the practical utility of the dataset, highlighting its potential to enhance SER performance when combined with classical feature extraction techniques and modern deep learning approaches. This study provides a valuable resource for future research and applications in fields such as edutainment and healthcare, with a focus on child-computer interactions.

articleTitle: Enhanced Real-Time Object Detection on Customized Dataset with YOLOv9 Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: YOLO has developed into a primary real-time object identification platform for applications such as video surveillance systems, autonomous vehicles, and robots. This research proposes an improved real-time object recognition approach based on the YOLOv9 architecture, trained on a football-specific custom dataset. The 255 annotated images in the dataset are separated into training, validation, and test sets with an 80-15-5 split ratio; there are 204 images in the training set, 38 in the validation set, and 13 in the test set. Our gelan-c model achieves remarkable detection performance with 467 layers, 25,414,044 parameters, and 102.5 GFLOPs. Upon validation, Gelan-c shows an aggregate mAP50 of 75.9%, with mAPs ranging from 32.2% (ball) to 93.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> (goalkeeper) depending on the specified class. The impressive aspect of the Gelan-C is its 31.6 ms picture processing rate, which assures real-time performance. The methodology covers environmental setup, preparation of data, YOLOv9 architecture introduction, and experimental evaluation to demonstrate the model's football-related recognition capabilities. The suggested approach has potential applications in sports event monitoring and evaluation due to its reliability and efficacy in detecting football players, referees, and the ball.

articleTitle: Inter-Subject Emotion Detection Using Empirical Mode Decomposition on EEG Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Accurate identification of human emotional states can be achieved through various methods, including subjective self-reports and obj ective measurements like facial expressions, vocal patterns, and physiological signals. Among these, use of physiological signal such as electroencephalogram (EEG) is optimal for emotion detection due to its direct measurement of brain activity, providing insights into neural processes underpinning emotions. However, detecting emotions using EEG signals is challenging in subj ect-independent scenarios, due to the fluctuating and unpredictable nature of these brain wave recordings. This study addresses these challenges by utilizing empirical mode decomposition (EMD) to analyze EEG signals. EMD is an iterative method that decomposes signals into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) without needing predefined basic functions. A 4-second sliding window with a 2-second overlap is utilized to divide the EEG signal into segments. Each segment is decomposed into five IMFs, and nonlinear features such as Shannon entropy, differential entropy, collision entropy, Hjorth parameters, and Higuchi's fractal dimension are extracted. These features serve as 2D inputs to an EEGN et classifier, a convolutional neural network designed for EEG signals. The study employs the DEAP dataset, which includes 32-channel EEG recordings from 32 participants who rated their arousal and valence levels after viewing music video excerpts. These ratings are mapped to high versus low arousal and valence categories. The study focuses on inter-subj ect emotion recognition and the findings from our experiments showcase average classification accuracies of 65.46% (±0.09 (SD)) for arousal and 62.5% (±0.06 (SD)) for valence in inter-subject emotion recognition.

articleTitle: Fractional Political Flower Pollination with DMN for Age-Related Macular Degeneration Detection Using OCT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: The eye disease that causes vision loss occurred for aged people is known as Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD). With the increase in aging population worldwide, there has been a growing prevalence in the number of incidence of AMD. Detection of AMD in the preliminary stages can aid in preventing loss of vision. Hence, this paper introduces a Fractional Political Flower Pollination Optimization-based Deep Maxout Network (FPFPO_DMN) method for the detection of AMD. At first, an input Optimal Coherence Tomography (OCT) image is considered as input and subjected to layer segmentation. Here, the retinal layers are segmented by employing ensemble U-Net, which is trained by Political Flower Pollination Optimization (PFPO). Then, feature extraction is executed for mining features, namely curvature, thickness, reflectivity, statistical features, and textual features. Then, AMD is detected with the help of the DMN, which is structurally optimized by introduced Fractional Political Flower Pollination Optimization (FPFPO) that is developed by the fusion of Fractional Calculus (FC) and PFPO. PFPO is developed by the combination of Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA) and Political Optimizer (PO). Further, the proposed FPFPO_DMN achieves better sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 0.940, 0.931, and 0.910.

articleTitle: Alzheimer's Disease Prediction Using Convolutional Neural Networks Pre Trained Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neu-rodegenerative disorder that significantly impacts memory and cognitive abilities. Accurate early-stage diagnosis is critical for implementing preventive measures before irreversible brain damage occurs. This paper presents a novel approach for AD prediction using convolutional neural networks (CNN) with pre-trained architectures, leveraging transfer learning to enhance classification accuracy. MRI scans from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset were used, categorized into three classes: AD (Alzheimer's Disease), CI (Mild Cognitive Impaired) and CN (Common Normal). The proposed method em-ploys pre-trained models such as VGG16, DenseNet121, Xception, ResNet152V2, NasNetLarge and InceptionResNetV2, fine-tuned for AD detection. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieved classification exceeding 90 % for precision and recall, highlighting the effectiveness of CNNs in handling large-scale medical data. These findings underscore the potential of deep learning models for supporting clinical diagnosis, reducing time and cost, and aiding in the early detection of Alzheimer's Disease

articleTitle: Convex Combination of Adaptive Filters for Channel Estimation of Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), power man-agement techniques and less power-consuming relay policies should be used to achieve improved quality of service (QoS) for the limited power supply, computational power, and memory capacity of sensor nodes. Most of these parameters are affected by the presence of modeling errors in the channel estimation process. Therefore, in this paper, a set of novel channel estimation algorithms that can achieve both faster convergence and smaller steady-state errors are designed to reduce the channel estimation error to improve the performance of WSNs.

articleTitle: Safeguarding Cryptocurrency Collateral for Value Preservation and Risk Mitigation in Volatile Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Recently, the cryptocurrency market has witnessed unprecedented growth and accompanying volatility surge, pre-senting a formidable challenge in upholding asset value and mitigating risks for digital asset holders. As the cryptocurrency domain advances, the imperative to fortify collateral and navigate risk assumes paramount importance for participants. This paper explores these pivotal concerns within the dynamic realm of Decentralized Finance (DeFi) platforms. The nucleus of this endeavor revolves around a meticulous investigation into applying options-based strategies as a bulwark against the tempestuous currents of the market. The primary aim is to shield and augment the value of cryptocurrency collateral amid the capricious throes of market volatility. The inquiry extends to probe the plausibility, efficacy, and ramifications inherent in harnessing options within DeFi platforms to realize the dual goals of conserving value and taming risk.

articleTitle: Blockchain Leveraging Trusted Vehicle Purchasing System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: In the automobile industry, many vehicles have an unknown history, so they may use scams and fraud. Leveraging Blockchain technology to securely store and manage vehicle purchase details and vehicle information to prevent fraud and provide conditional privacy. Transactions of vehicles are recorded on the Blockchain, guaranteeing data integrity and immutability through another cryptographic hashing function. The paper also explores interoperability with other Blockchain systems and scalability solutions for increasing transaction volumes. Future scope of improvements will involve adopting a more secure hashing algorithm, integrating smart contracts to automate trans-actions, and creating a user-friendly, decentralized application for the system interaction. This work highlights the transformative potential of blockchain technology in revolutionizing secure data management within the automotive industry. The empirical results prove the efficacy of the proposed system.

articleTitle: DR Image Super-Resolution Using Deep Hybrid Feature Based Nested Attention Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of vision disability leading to blindness, thus early and precise diagnosis through high-resolution retinal images can prevent vision loss. However, generating high-resolution images is challenging due to low resolution in the spatial and spectral domains, noise, imaging artifacts, and sometimes hardware limitations. This study proposed a deep hybrid feature-based nested attention approach for super-resolving DR images, enhancing image quality and detail. The method combines proposed deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and super-resolution networks (SRN) to reconstruct HR images from LR. The model captures complex retinal structures by integrating global and local feature extraction, enhancing image resolution and diagnostic accuracy. This proposed model reconstructs high-resolution diabetic retinopathy (DR) images of dimensions (128 × 128) from low-resolution images of size (32 × 32). The higher PSNR and SSIM values obtained during the experiment on the public APTOS 2019 Blindness Detection dataset show the model's ability to preserve details and minimize artifacts for reliable diabetic retinopathy (DR) diagnosis. This research aims to assist in screening and diagnosis for early detection of DR.

articleTitle: Stock Market Prediction Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT)
abstract: This project focuses on leveraging One kind of deep learning model is the Long Short-Term Memory (LS TM) networks., to forecast stock prices by analyzing historical data and technical indicators. The methodology involves comprehensive steps such as data collection, preprocessing, feature selection, model selection (including LSTM networks), training, and evaluation taking advantage of performance indicators such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). It utilizes a dataset comprising historical gold stock prices and trading volume to train and test the LSTM model. Furthermore, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Linear Regression, and other machine learning algorithms are examined in the study, along with more complex methods like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Results reveal diverse accuracy levels across models, with LSTM demonstrating a tendency to overpredict stock prices. Future endeavors aim to refine model performance, investigate ensemble methods, and integrate additional data sources like economic news and sentiment analysis to bolster prediction accuracy, thereby offering investors and analysts enhanced decision-making tools in the dynamic stock market landscape.
